ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.claim: The fate of a wealthy Jewish capitalist shows that God grants favors, though the wretched attribute them to their own ability and idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.anchor: The fate of a capitalist Jew is mentioned.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r9.claim: The word ʿilm is a verbal noun that may be construed as knowledge belonging to Qārūn or as knowledge from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r9.anchor: على علم، علم: مصدر، يحتمل أن يكون مضافا إليه ومضافا إلى الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r10.claim: Most commentators say Qārūn claimed his knowledge entitled him to the treasures; one view identifies it with Torah learning and selection among Moses's seventy delegates, but calls that sophistry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r10.anchor: فقال الجمهور: ادعى أن عنده علما استوجب به أن يكون صاحب تلك الكنوز.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r11.speaker: أبو سليمان الداني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r11.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dānī takes the claimed knowledge as commerce and methods of earning: Qārūn says his own intelligence and effort gained the wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r11.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداني: أي علم التجارة ووجوه المكاسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r12.speaker: ابن المسيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r12.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib identifies the knowledge as alchemy; a report says Moses knew it as transmuting lead and copper into gold.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r13.claim: Alchemy is also attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās as knowledge of the craft, but the author doubts these attributions and cites al-Zajjāj's denial of alchemy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: على علم الصنعة الذهب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r1.claim: The author criticizes Egyptian seekers of alchemy and similar impossibilities, noting that even their religious elders solicit such claims from ignorant visitors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r1.anchor: وكثيرا ما تولع أهل مصر بطلب أشياء من المستحيلات والخرافات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say Qārūn claimed God had specially selected him for the wealth, so he owed nothing to his critics.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r2.anchor:
وقال ابن زيد وغيره: أراد:
أوتيته على علم من الله وتخصيص من لدنه قصدني به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r3.claim: Muqātil glosses the claim as wealth given on account of good that God knew Qārūn possessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r3.anchor:
وقال مقاتل:
على علم، أي على خير علمه الله عندي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r4.claim: “Did he not know?” reminds Qārūn that stronger and richer earlier peoples were destroyed; he could know this from Torah, Moses, or histories and should not trust his wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: أولم يعلم، تقرير لعلمه ذلك، وتنبيه على خطئه في اغتراره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī asks whether Qārūn possessed this useful knowledge of how to avoid the fate of those destroyed, despite boasting of knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون نعتا لعلمه بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r6.claim: “Greater in gathering” may mean greater wealth or more people to protect and serve; Ibn ʿAtiyya says the wording reinforces Qārūn's self-conceit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r6.anchor: وأكثر جمعا، إما للمال، أو جماعة يحوطونه ويخدمونه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb connects the passive “they are not asked about their sins” to the preceding destruction: God did not need to ask the destroyed peoples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r7.anchor: قاله محمد بن كعب. والضمير في ذنوبهم عائد على من أهلك من القرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r8.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r8.claim: Qatāda says the destroyed are not asked because God already knows their sins; elsewhere he says the guilty's sins are obvious and they enter Hell without reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p326/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم لظهورها وكثرتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the phrase as a prohibition addressed to the Prophet, with “the guilty” in the accusative; Ibn Sīrīn and Abū al-ʿĀliya likewise read the prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر في روايته: ولا تسأل، بالتاء والجزم، المجرمين: نصب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq allows the prohibitive reading only if al-mujrimīn is accusative as the verb's object; the author discusses alternatives if it remains nominative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r3.anchor: وكان ابن أبي إسحاق لا يجوز ذلك إلا إن يكون المجرمين بالياء في محل النصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r4.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r4.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ offers a nominative analysis by supplying a subject or treating the noun as a return to the underlying case of the pronoun; the author says the analogous reading lacks evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r4.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح: فالظاهر ما قاله، ولم يبلغني في نصب المجرمين شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r5.claim: Qatāda and Mujāhid say angels recognize sinners from their dark, disfigured signs, as in 55:41; another view says this is not a question of reproach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p327/r5.anchor: لا تسألهم الملائكة عن ذنوبهم، لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم من السواد والتشويه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.claim: Razi says this admonition was already complete and could not be improved, yet Qarun refused it and answered with ingratitude by claiming his wealth came from his own knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.anchor: ما لو قيل لم يكن عليه مزيد

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r14.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r14.claim: Qatadah, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi say Qarun was Israel's foremost Torah scholar and claimed his learning and merit entitled him to the wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r14.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي : كان قارون أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r15.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r15.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Dahhak say Moses received alchemical knowledge from heaven and divided it among Qarun, Joshua, and Caleb; Qarun tricked the others, took their shares, and transmuted lead to silver and copper to gold.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r15.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك : كان موسى عليه السلام أنزل عليه علم الكيمياء

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r16.claim: A third interpretation takes Qarun to mean that his expertise in commerce and methods of earning produced his wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r16.anchor: أراد به علمه بوجوه المكاسب والتجارات

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r17.claim: A fourth reading says God gave Qarun wealth while knowing his circumstances, which he takes to prove it was good for him; عندي means 'in my view' or belief.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r17.anchor: الله أعطاني ذلك مع كونه عالما بي وبأحوالي

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r18.claim: The rhetorical question may affirm Qarun knew from the Torah, Moses, and historical transmitters that God had destroyed stronger and richer peoples, yet he still boasted of his own resources.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r18.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا إثباتا لعلمه بأن الله تعالى قد أهلك قبله

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r19.claim: Alternatively, the question denies that Qarun possessed useful knowledge: he claimed knowledge made him deserve every blessing but lacked knowledge that could guard him from the fate of the destroyed.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r19.anchor: يجوز أن يكون نفيا لعلمه بذلك كأنه لما قال أوتيته على علم عندي

RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r1.claim: جمعا may mean a greater accumulation of wealth or a larger gathering and number of people.
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r1.anchor: فالمعنى أكثر جمعا للمال أو أكثر جماعة وعددا

RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r2.claim: The answer is that Qarun's confidence in wealth, strength, and supporters was deeply mistaken: when God wills his destruction, none of these resources, however multiplied, can help.
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r2.anchor: وحاصل الجواب أن اغتراره بماله وقوته وجموعه من الخطأ العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r3.claim: God needs no inquiry into the nature or extent of criminals' sins when punishing them, because He already knows everything.
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r3.anchor: لأنه تعالى عالم بكل المعلومات فلا حاجة به إلى السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r4.claim: Razi reconciles this with the promise to question everyone in 15:92 by assigning the verses to two different times, as he explains elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r4.anchor: قلنا يحمل ذلك على وقتين على ما قررناه

RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r5.claim: Abu Muslim distinguishes questioning for accounting, reproach, or seeking an opportunity to make amends; the last is most apt here, as other verses say disbelievers are denied it and cannot excuse themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v25p15/r5.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم وجها آخر فقال : السؤال قد يكون للمحاسبة

BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r5.claim: Qarun's reply refers to the wealth he has received.

BURSEVI:v6p314/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314/r1.claim: The phrase ʿalā ʿilmin ʿindī may be a circumstantial phrase attached to the subject of ūtītuhu, or it may modify ūtītuhu, with ʿindī adjectival to ʿilm.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r1.anchor: حال من مرفوع أوتيته أو متعلق بأوتيته وعندي صفة له

BURSEVI:v6p314/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314/r2.claim: Qarun claims his Torah knowledge made him deserving of wealth and superiority, overlooking God's favor; all who boast of merit and deny grace will eventually perish for their disobedience.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r2.anchor: أوتيته حال كوني مستحقا لما في من علم التوراة وكان أعلمهم بها ادعى استحقاق التفضيل

BURSEVI:v6p314/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r3.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v6p314/r3.claim: Hafez warns the jurist not to pride himself on knowledge or deeds, since no one escapes God's decree.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r3.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
مباش غره بعلم وعمل فقيه مدام

BURSEVI:v6p314/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r4.speaker: الصائب
BURSEVI:v6p314/r4.claim: Saib's verse says the proud never reflect on nonexistence, despite its shears poised at their collars.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r4.anchor:
وقال الصائب :
431
بفكر نيستي هركز نمي فتند مغروران

BURSEVI:v6p314/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p314/r5.claim: One view identifies Qarun's claimed knowledge as alchemy: Moses learned it from God and taught one third each to Joshua and Caleb, while Qarun tricked them and combined their knowledge.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بعلم علم الكيمياء وكان موسى يعلمه تعلما من الله تعالى فعلم يوشع بن نون ثلث ذلك العلم

BURSEVI:v6p314/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p314/r6.claim: Another account says Qarun learned alchemy from Moses' sister Kulthum and made immense wealth by turning lead to silver and copper to gold.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r6.anchor: أو تعلم قارون صنعة الكيمياء من كلثوم أخت موسى وكانت تعرف ذلك فرزق مالا عظيما

BURSEVI:v6p314/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r7.speaker: الزجاج
BURSEVI:v6p314/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj holds that alchemy has no reality.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج : علم الكيمياء لا حقيقة له

BURSEVI:v6p314/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r8.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v6p314/r8.claim: Al-Kawashi says practitioners of alchemy are mostly liars and should not be trusted.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r8.anchor: وفي "الكواشي" : ومتعاطي هذا العلم الكثير كذبه فلا يلتفت إليه

BURSEVI:v6p314/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314/r9.claim: The author prefers a qualified belief that alchemy is real over al-Zajjaj's rejection: purification can transform bodies, and prophets and perfected saints have practiced it; he says he has witnessed its attainment.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r9.anchor: يقول الفقير : وهو أولى من قول الزجاج فإن فيه إقرارا بأصله في الجملة

BURSEVI:v6p314/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p314/r10.claim: Another explanation takes the knowledge to be commerce, farming, and other livelihoods; a story says Qarun's piety was gradually redirected by Iblis into work and attachment to wealth, ending in his claim to deserve riches through his business skill.
BURSEVI:v6p314/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بالعلم علم التجارة والدهقنة وسائر المكاسب

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r1.claim: The question asks whether Qarun knew that God had already destroyed earlier unbelieving generations.
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r1.anchor: أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r2.claim: A qarn is a people living together in the same period.
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r2.anchor: والقرن القوم المقترنون في زمن واحد

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r3.claim: The previous peoples surpassed Qarun in strength through their numbers and equipment.

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r4.claim: They also had greater wealth, as in the case of Nimrod and others.

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r5.claim: Some say they had amassed more knowledge and worship, like Iblis.
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وأكثر جمعا للعلم والطاعة مثل إبليس

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r6.claim: Exegetes take the verse as God's rebuke of Qarun's conceit in his strength and wealth despite what he knew of earlier destruction, learned from the Torah, Moses, and transmitters of history.

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r7.claim: The point is that Qarun should have read the Torah and learned what God did to similar former peoples, so he would not have been conceited.
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r7.anchor: فالمعنى ألم يقرأ التوراة ويعلم ما فعل الله بأضرابه من أهل القرون السابقة

BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r8.claim: The Persian couplet warns against relying on property, wealth, and a large household, since people before and after us have been greater; learn from past generations.
BURSEVI:v6p314#2/r8.anchor: مكن تكيه بر ملك واه وحشم كه يش ازتو بودست وبعد از توهم بكير عبرت از ماسواي قرون

BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r1.claim: At destruction, the criminals are not asked about their sins so they cannot delay matters with excuses.

BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says they are not questioned for information on Judgment Day, since God already knows their sins, but are questioned to reproach and humiliate them.
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : لا يسألون يوم القيامة سؤال استعلام فإنه تعالى مطلع عليها بل يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r3.claim: Others say they are punished immediately without pause or reckoning, or are not asked because angels recognize them by their marks.
BURSEVI:v6p314#3/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا يسألون بل يعاقبون بلا توقف ولا حساب أو لا يسألون لأنهم تعرفهم الملائكة بسيماهم

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r1.claim: Korah attributes his blessings to knowledge he possesses, rather than acknowledging them as divine gifts.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r1.anchor: it is clear that Korah attributes the blessings he possesses to knowledge he has

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r2.claim: Some commentators explain Korah’s wealth through particular skills; accounts call him a goldsmith or alchemist, though commentators mention and dismiss both accounts.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r2.anchor: Some say he was a goldsmith; others transmit a tradition that he was an alchemist, which are both mentioned and dismissed by commentators

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r3.claim: Elsewhere ʿalā ʿilm can mean that God acts on the basis of His Knowledge; its sense in other cases remains open to interpretation.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r3.anchor: in other instances this phrase can also be used to mean that God acts based upon His Knowledge

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r4.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r4.claim: Some commentators take ʿindī to mean “in my opinion,” yielding “given on account of knowledge, in my opinion.”
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r4.anchor: the word and which would make the translation, “I have only been given it on account of knowledge, in my opinion”(R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r5.claim: The warning about earlier peoples as strong or wealthy as Korah who were destroyed recurs in several verses.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r5.anchor: Other verses in which disbelievers are reminded of those generations or peoples who came before them

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r6.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r6.claim: One reading is that the guilty of one generation are not questioned about or held responsible for another generation’s sins.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r6.anchor: the guilty of one generation will not be questioned about or held responsible for the sins of another generation (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r7.claim: The statement can mean that the guilty cannot make amends or obtain favor, paralleling 30:57 and 41:24.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r7.anchor: Nor can they make amends (Q); and 41:24: And if they seek favor, they will not be granted favor

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r8.claim: God has no need to question the guilty about their deeds because He already knows them completely.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r8.anchor: God has no need to question them about their deeds, because He already knows these deeds completely (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r9.claim: To reconcile this with 15:92, some distinguish questions seeking information, calling to account, or rebuking; God questions people in one respect, not another.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r9.anchor: different kinds of questions to be asked—those that seek information, those that call one to account, and those that are meant as rebuke (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:78/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r10.speaker: Sufis
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r10.claim: Sufis counsel against exulting in one’s attainments or taking pride in one’s states, words, or deeds; such self-glorification marks a wretched person.
STUDYQURAN:28:78/r10.anchor: According to the Sufis, one should not exult in one’s own attainments or be pleased with one’s own state

TAB-FULL:v18p325/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r1.claim: Qarun claims that his treasures were given because God knew his merit and favored him over others for his superior knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r1.anchor: علمه الله مني، فرضي بذلك عني، وفضلني بهذا المال عليكم

TAB-FULL:v18p325/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses Qarun’s claim as receiving the wealth on the basis of knowledge or information he possessed.
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " { قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} [القصص: 78] قال: على خبر عندي

TAB-FULL:v18p325/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun meant that God’s gift proved divine approval of him and recognition of his merit.
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} [القصص: 78] قال: لولا رضا الله عني ومعرفته بفضلي ما أعطاني هذا

TAB-FULL:v18p325/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r4.claim: An alternative gloss takes عندي to mean ‘as I see it’: Qarun says his knowledge is superior, in his own estimation.
TAB-FULL:v18p325/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى قوله: {عندي} [الأنعام: 50] بمعنى: أرى، كأنه قال: إنما أوتيته لفضل علمي، فيما أرى

TAB-FULL:v18p326/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p326/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p326/r1.claim: Qarun should know that stronger and wealthier peoples were destroyed; if wealth proved merit and God’s approval, God would not have destroyed them, since He destroys those with whom He is displeased.
TAB-FULL:v18p326/r1.anchor: بطشا، وأكثر جمعا للأموال؛ ولو كان الله يؤتي الأموال من يؤتيه

TAB-FULL:v18p327/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r1.claim: Qatadah explains that the guilty enter Hell without being subjected to an accounting.
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} [القصص: 78] قال: يدخلون النار بغير حساب "

TAB-FULL:v18p327/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r2.claim: Mujahid says the angels do not question the criminals because they recognize them by their marks, as in 55:41; they have blue, blackened faces.
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} [القصص: 78] كقوله: {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} [الرحمن: 41] زرقا سود الوجوه

TAB-FULL:v18p327/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb takes the pronoun to concern earlier peoples: later criminals will not be asked why those past nations were destroyed.
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب، " {ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} [القصص: 78] قال: عن ذنوب الذين مضوا فيم أهلكوا

TAB-FULL:v18p327/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the pronoun to refer to the criminals themselves, not the earlier generations: God does not ask an innocent person, believer or unbeliever, about another’s sin.
TAB-FULL:v18p327/r4.anchor: وهي بأن تكون من ذكر المجرمين أولى، لأن الله تعالى ذكره غير سائل عن ذنوب مذنب غير من أذنب، لا مؤمن ولا كافر

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r7.claim: Qarun answers all the advice by denying his wealth was an undeserved divine favor and claiming he earned it through superior knowledge of acquiring and managing wealth; he therefore thinks he may use it for luxury, power, and ambition.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r7.anchor: وكان كلامهم مبنيا على أن ماله من الثروة إنما آتاه الله إحسانا إليه وفضلا منه من غير استيجاب واستحقاق فيجب عليه

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r8.claim: Qarun’s self-crediting conceit is common among worldly people: they attribute wealth and power to their own ability, knowledge, and expertise, overlooking destiny and outward circumstances.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r8.anchor: لا يرى الواحد منهم فيما ساقه إليه التقدير ووافقته الأسباب الظاهرة من عزة عاجلة وقوة مستعارة إلا أن نفسه هي الفاعلة له

TABATABAI:28:78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78/r1.claim: The surrounding parallels in 39:52 and 40:82–83 confirm that Qarun means know-how for acquiring wealth, as explained earlier.
TABATABAI:28:78/r1.anchor: وعرض الآيات على قصة قارون لا يبقي شكا في أن المراد بالعلم في كلامه ما قدمناه

TABATABAI:28:78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78/r2.claim: By saying he was given wealth without naming God as giver, Qarun turns away from mentioning God and disparages divine majesty.
TABATABAI:28:78/r2.anchor: من غير إسناد الإيتاء إلى الله سبحانه كما في قول الناصحين له

TABATABAI:28:78/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78/r3.claim: The question rebukes Qarun with the simplest refutation: stronger, more numerous earlier peoples also had wealth by their own knowledge, yet God destroyed them for sin; if knowledge secured wealth and safety, they would have survived and kept it.

TABATABAI:28:78/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78/r4.claim: In context this describes God's practice of punishing criminals without delay or hearing fabricated excuses: He knows the facts and brings an irresistible punishment suddenly, unlike human rulers who question offenders.
TABATABAI:28:78/r4.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن المراد به بيان السنة الإلهية في تعذيب المجرمين وإهلاكهم بذنوبهم

TABATABAI:28:78/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78/r5.claim: One reported interpretation takes the knowledge to be Torah learning, since Qarun was the most learned Israelite in the Torah.

TABATABAI:28:78/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78/r6.claim: Another view identifies the knowledge as alchemy, which Qarun learned from Moses, Joshua son of Nun, and Caleb son of Jephunneh; he alone possessed it.
TABATABAI:28:78/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد علم الكيمياء وكان قد تعلمه من موسى ويوشع بن نون وكالب بن يوقنا

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r1.claim: A further view says Qarun knew how to extract buried treasures and had brought out many such treasures.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r1.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعلم علم استخراج الكنوز والدفائن وقد استخرج به كنوزا ودفائن كثيرة

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r2.claim: One view takes the knowledge as God's knowledge and the gift as a special divine choice of Qarun; عندي expresses what he thought.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعلم علم الله تعالى والمعنى أوتيته على علم من الله وتخصيص منه قصدني به

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r3.claim: Another view also takes knowledge as God's knowledge, but in the sense of what He knew: the gift was based on good He knew to be in Qarun.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r3.anchor: وقيل العلم علم الله لكنه بمعنى المعلوم

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r4.claim: Across these interpretations, على can indicate superiority; some also allow it to mean because of or on account of.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r4.anchor: على جميع هذه الأقوال للاستعلاء وجوز أن تكون

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r5.claim: One reading places the negated question at Judgment: it is not an inquiry for information, since God knows their sins and angels know them from records and their marks; 37:24 is questioning for reproach instead.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r5.anchor: سؤال يوم القيامة والمنفي سؤال الاستعلام

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r6.claim: A proposed reconciliation gives the question the same sense in both passages, but says it occurs at one Judgment station and is absent at another.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r6.anchor: ويمكن إن يكون السؤال في الآيتين بمعنى واحد والنفي والإثبات باعتبار اختلاف المواقف يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r7.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the stronger people destroyed earlier and takes the criminals as different people, who are not asked about those earlier people's sins.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r7.anchor: والمراد بالمجرمين غيرهم والمعنى لا يسأل عن ذنوب

TABATABAI:28:78-80/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r8.claim: The alternative readings of the question do not fit the immediate context, which completes the rebuke of Qarun's claim that his knowledge made him wealthy.
TABATABAI:28:78-80/r8.anchor: وهذه كلها وجوه من التفسير لا يلائمها السياق

TABRISI:28:77-78/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r11.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:77-78/r11.claim: Qatāda says Qarun claimed superior knowledge and merit, supposing the wealth was God’s reward for his distinction, like the boast in 18:36.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r11.anchor: عن قتادة يعني أنه قدر أن هذا ثواب من الله له لفضيلته

TABRISI:28:77-78/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:28:77-78/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun meant God favored him because He knew he deserved the wealth; this is close to Qatāda’s view.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه لرضا الله عني ومعرفته باستحقاقي عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:28:77-78/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r13.claim: Another view is that Qarun meant specialized knowledge of trade, agriculture, and other ways of making wealth unavailable to others.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r13.anchor: المال حصل له على علم عندي بوجوه المكاسب وبما لا يتهيأ لأحد

TABRISI:28:77-78/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r14.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:28:77-78/r14.claim: Al-Kalbī says Qarun claimed knowledge of gold-making or alchemy; a story says Moses, Joshua, and Aaron’s son each taught him a third, and Qarun tricked them into revealing all three.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r14.anchor: وهو علم الكيمياء عن الكلبي وحكي أن موسى ع علم قارون الثلث

TABRISI:28:77-78/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r15.claim: God destroyed unbelieving generations stronger and wealthier than Qarun, including ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Lot’s people; wealth could not save them from punishment.

TABRISI:28:79-81/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:79-81/r1.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:79-81/r1.claim: Qatāda says criminals enter Hell without being called to account.
TABRISI:28:79-81/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني أنهم يدخلون النار بغير حساب

TABRISI:28:79-81/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:79-81/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:79-81/r2.claim: Qatāda also says angels recognize criminals by their marks, seize them by forelocks and feet, and drive them to Hell, as in 55:39.
TABRISI:28:79-81/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن الملائكة تعرفهم بسيماهم

TABRISI:28:79-81/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:79-81/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:28:79-81/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reconciles this with 15:92: that questioning is rebuke and reproach, not a request for information.
TABRISI:28:79-81/r3.anchor: لا ليعلم ذلك من قبلهم عن الحسن

THALABI:v7p262/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p262/r2.claim: Qarun claims he received his wealth through superior knowledge God gave him, considers himself worthy of it, and says his knowledge and other qualities make him superior.
THALABI:v7p262/r2.anchor: على فضل علم عندي علمنيه الله، ورآني لذلك أهلا، ففضلني بهذا المال عليكم لفضلي عليكم بالعلم وغيره

THALABI:v7p262/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v7p262/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab says Moses knew alchemy and taught a third each to Joshua, Caleb, and Qarun; Qarun tricked the other two into combining their knowledge with his.
THALABI:v7p262/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: كان موسى (عليه السلام) يعلم الكيمياء

THALABI:v7p262/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p262/r4.claim: Another report says God taught Moses alchemy, Moses taught his sister, and she taught Qarun, prompting his claim about his knowledge.
THALABI:v7p262/r4.anchor: وفي خبر آخر أن الله سبحانه وتعالى علم موسى علم الكيمياء، فعلم موسى أخته، فعلمت أخته قارون

THALABI:v7p262/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p262/r5.claim: A further view understands the knowledge as expertise in trade, agriculture, and all kinds of earning and acquisition.
THALABI:v7p262/r5.anchor: وقيل: على علم عندي بالتصرف في التجارات والزراعات وسائر أنواع المكاسب والمطالب

THALABI:v7p262/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r6.speaker: أبو سلمان الداراني
THALABI:v7p262/r6.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani recounts that Qarun worshipped for forty years; Iblis outdid him in worship, gradually persuaded him to abandon communal and charitable duties, then to alternate work and worship, after which worldly wealth poured in.
THALABI:v7p262/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا سلمان الداراني يقول: يبدي إبليس لقارون

THALABI:v7p262#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p262#2/r1.claim: God reminds Qarun that earlier unbelieving generations stronger and richer than he had already been destroyed.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r1.anchor: أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون الكافرة من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا

THALABI:v7p262#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p262#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the criminals enter Hell without reckoning.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: يدخلون النار بغير حساب

THALABI:v7p262#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p262#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the angels do not ask the criminals because they recognize them by their distinguishing marks.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r3.anchor: مجاهد: يعني: إن الملائكة لا تسأل عنهم لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيمائهم

THALABI:v7p262#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p262#2/r4.claim: Hasan says others already know their sins; any questioning is for reproach and rebuke, not to obtain information.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r4.anchor: الحسن: لا يسئل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون ليعلم ذلك من قبلهم فأن سئلوا سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says Qarun claimed his wealth had been granted because of his knowledge of the Torah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ادعى أنه أعطي المال لعلمه بالتوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads علم as merit: Qarun claimed he deserved the wealth because of his superior knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: على فضل عندي، أي: كنت أهله ومستحقا له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r3.claim: A report says Qarun was Israel’s most learned reader of the Torah and claimed the wealth showed God’s preference for his learning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r3.anchor: ويروى أنه كان أقرأ رجل في بني إسرائيل للتوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r4.claim: Muqātil similarly interprets Qarun as claiming he possessed goodness and knowledge recognized by God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r4.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مقاتل: على خير علمه الله عندي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r5.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says Qarun disbelieved by crediting wealth to his own skill and acquisitions rather than God’s gift.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} فكفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r6.claim: Through ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith contrasts Solomon’s attribution of his gift to God’s grace with Qarun’s attribution of wealth to himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r6.anchor: ما روى علي بن زيد بن جدعان، عن عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s interpretation that Qarun meant his skill in making gold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قال ابن عباس: {على علم عندي} بصنعة الذهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects the report that Qarun practiced alchemy because alchemy is false and has no reality.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: والذي روي أنه كان يعمل الكيمياء لا يصح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r9.claim: God destroyed earlier communities for denying their messengers, including people stronger than Qarun and richer in amassed wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r9.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {أولم يعلم} قارون {أن الله قد أهلك} بالعذاب {من قبله من القرون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify Nimrod ibn Canaan, the tyrant, among the stronger and wealthier earlier figures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يريد نمروذ بن كنعان، الجبار، وغيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r1.claim: Mujāhid says angels do not question the criminals, recognizing them by their blue appearance and black faces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: الملائكة لا تسأل عنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says unbelievers are not questioned because each is recognizable by a sign; al-Farrāʾ prefers this view and cites 55:39 and 55:41.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لا يسأل الكافر عن ذنبه، كل معروف بسيماه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ links recognition by signs to the verses saying criminals are known by their marks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r3.anchor: كما قال: {فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه} الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī rejects that explanation: the question is not asked to identify them; the wording would need to say criminals are not questioned for that sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r4.anchor: وهذا القول لا يصح؛ لأن سؤالهم عن ذنوبهم ليس لمعرفتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls Qatāda’s explanation correct: criminals enter Hell without reckoning; questioning elsewhere can be for rebuke, as at 15:92 and al-Ḥasan explains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r5.anchor: والصحيح ما قال قتادة؛ قال: إنهم يدخلون النار بغير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says any questioning is for reproach and rebuke, not to learn what God already knows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r6.anchor: كما قال الحسن في هذه الآية: لا يسألون ليعلم ذلك من قبلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r7.claim: The scholars of meaning say they are not asked as someone who might offer an excuse that removes blame would be questioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: {يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} سؤال من لعل له عذرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r8.claim: Muqātil says criminals of this community are not questioned about the sins of past nations punished in the world, which God recorded; al-Wāḥidī calls this weak.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول لا يسأل مجرمو هذه الأمة عن ذنوب الأمم الخالية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r9.claim: On Muqātil’s reading, the pronoun in their sins refers to nations destroyed earlier rather than the criminals; al-Wāḥidī says this interpretation is weak.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p461/r9.anchor: وعلى هذا القول الكناية في: {ذنوبهم} لا تعود

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r5.claim: Qarun claims that his knowledge makes him deserving of his wealth; he was the most learned Israelite in the Torah.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r5.anchor: على فضل علم عندي، وكنت بذلك العلم مسحقا لفضل المال، وكان أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r6.claim: God had destroyed earlier generations stronger than Qarun and greater in amassed wealth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r6.anchor: من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا } للمال منه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r7.claim: The criminals enter the Fire without being called to account.

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r5.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r5.claim: Some interpret Qarun's claim of knowledge as referring to his knowledge of trade and economics.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r5.anchor: bu ilme bazıları ticaret ve iktisad ilmi demişler

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r6.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r6.claim: Others interpret the knowledge Qarun claimed to possess as alchemy.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r6.anchor: iktisad ilmi demişler, bazıları da el-kimya demişler.

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r7.claim: Even if Qarun's wealth came solely from his knowledge, he should have learned that God destroyed earlier people stronger and richer than him, such as Pharaoh; why did he not benefit from that knowledge?
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r7.anchor: ile olsa kurûn-ı ûlâ içinde ondan daha kuvvetli ve daha çok servetli (Firavun gibi) kimseleri helâk etmiş olduğunu bilmiyor muydu?

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r8.claim: Criminals need not be questioned to establish their guilt: God knows them, and angels recognize them by their faces and seize them immediately, as 55:41 says.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r8.anchor: meleklerce de sîmalarından bilinir ve derhâl yaka paça tutulurlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r1.claim: The statement that guilty people will not be asked does not mean they escape accountability or are sent to hell without reckoning; their crimes and ruinous fate are already manifest, making this a stern warning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r1.anchor: Bu ifade, söz konusu suçluların yapıp ettiklerinin suç ve günah olduğunun âşikâr olarak bilinmesi sebebiyle akıbetlerinin de bir felâket olduğunun apaçık gerçek olarak bilindiği anlamına gelmekte

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r1.claim: A skilled prose writer recognizes the structure and movement of his own writing, just as an experienced poet recognizes each poet's natural style.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r1.anchor: مترسل في رسالته فهو لا يخفى عليه بناء قاعدته وأساسه فكأنه يرى انه عليه مجاري حركاته

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r2.claim: Some Quranic expressions are closed or allusive; when they convey as much as explicit explanation while satisfying its demands, they reach the highest degree of meaning.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r2.anchor: فمنها الكلام المغلق والإشارات وإذا بلغ الكلام من هذا القبيل مبلغا ربما زاد الإفهام به على الإيضاح

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r3.claim: The arrangement of the Night Journey verse is exceptionally eloquent and subtle in its ordering and in containing a momentous event and exalted station.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r3.anchor: فصول هذه الآية وكلماتها على ما شرحنا من قبل البلاغة واللطف في التقدم وفي تضمن هذا الأمر العظيم

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r4.claim: The move from the Night Journey to the statement about Moses might seem disconnected elsewhere, but Quranic composition makes the transition seamless.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r4.anchor: ويتلو هذه قوله ( ﴿ وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ﴾ ) هذا خروج

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r5.claim: The transition from Israel's descendants to Noah suits the cadence and turns naturally into praise of his gratitude; their descent from him calls them to follow his gratitude and exclusive trust in God.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r5.anchor: ثم أنظر كيف أجري هذا الخطاب إلى ذكر نوح وكيف أثنى عليه وكيف تليق صفته بالفاصلة ويتم النظم بها

BAQILLANI:v1p209/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r6.claim: The passage recalls Noah's descendants' deliverance through the flood, explains past punishment as due to their sins, and warns that renewed ignorance and rebellion bring punishment again.
BAQILLANI:v1p209/r6.anchor: أن يشكروا كشكره ولا يتخذوا من دون الله وكيلا وأن يعتقدوا تعظيم تخليصه إياهم من الطوفان

BURHAN:v4p24/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p24/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p24/r7.claim: A pronoun may anticipate an antecedent that is delayed in wording but already present in the intended meaning, as with fear and the criminals' sins.
BURHAN:v4p24/r7.anchor: الثاني أن يعود على مذكور في سياق الكلام مؤخر في اللفظ مقدم في النية

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r10.claim: Self-admiration is ruinous; the deadly poison is looking at oneself as independently real and imagining that one possesses any power of negation or affirmation.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r10.anchor: ما لاحظ أحد نفسه إلا هلك بإعجابه . ويقال السم القاتل ، والذي يطفئ السراج المضيء النظر إلى النفس بعين الإثبات

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.claim: A pronoun may precede its matching antecedent in wording while the antecedent is not later in syntactic rank, as in these examples.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.anchor: أو متأخرا لفظا لا رتبة مطابقا نحو ﴿ فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى ﴾ ﴿ ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون ﴾

SULAMI:v2p110#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r1.claim: Sahl says self-regard and claiming a spiritual state prevent flourishing or attaining that state.
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل رحمة الله عليه : ما نظر أحد إلى نفسه فأفلح ولا ادعى لنفسه حالا فتمت

SULAMI:v2p110#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r2.claim: The fortunate turn from their own deeds and words to divine grace; the wretched admire and claim their works, whose poison eventually destroys them.
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r2.anchor: والسعيد من الخلق من صرف بصره عن أفعاله وأقواله وفتح له سبيل الفضل والأفضال ورؤية منة الله عليه

SULAMI:v2p110#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r3.claim: Sahl reads Qarun’s claim as forgetting grace and claiming merit; outward destruction mirrors the inward loss of divine protection, reliance on one’s own power, boastfulness, blindness to grace, and ingratitude.
SULAMI:v2p110#2/r3.anchor: نسى الفضل وادعاها لنفسه فضلا فخسف الله به الأرض ظاهرا فكم قد خسف بالأسرار وصاحبها لا يشعر بذلك

ITQAN:v1p273/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p273/r1.speaker: ابن خير
ITQAN:v1p273/r1.claim: Ibn Khayr claims consensus that no one may transmit a hadith from the Prophet without having received it by narration or authorization.
ITQAN:v1p273/r1.anchor: ادعى ابن خير الإجماع على أنه ليس لأحد أن ينقل حديثا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما لم يكن له به رواية

ITQAN:v1p273/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p273/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p273/r2.claim: The author finds no report requiring Qur'an transmission through a teacher: stricter caution is plausible, but hadith rules guard against additions and false attribution, whereas the Qur'an is preserved, widely received, and readily transmitted; this is the apparent view.
ITQAN:v1p273/r2.anchor: ولعدم اشتراطه فيه وجه من حيث أن اشتراط ذلك في الحديث وإنما هو لخوف أن يدخل في الحديث ما ليس منه

TUSTARI:28:78/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:78/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:78/r1.claim: No one prospers by gazing at himself or succeeds by claiming a spiritual state for himself.
TUSTARI:28:78/r1.anchor: ما نظر إلى نفسه أحد فأفلح، ولا ادعى لنفسه حالا فتم له

TUSTARI:28:78/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:78/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:78/r2.claim: The fortunate turn from their own states and deeds to God's favor in every action; the wretched boast of their own qualities and deeds, inviting ruin.
TUSTARI:28:78/r2.anchor: والسعيد من الخلق من صرف بصره عن أحواله، وأفعاله سبيل الفضل والإفضال،

TUSTARI:28:78/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:78/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:78/r3.claim: Sahl understands Qarun's claim as a claim to merit: Qarun was the best reader of the Torah, and God visibly sank him.
TUSTARI:28:78/r3.anchor: يعني الفضل، وهو أنه كان أقرأهم للتوراة، فادعى لنفسه فضلا، فخسف الله به الأرض ظاهرا

TUSTARI:28:78/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:78/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:78/r4.claim: A person's inward sinking is loss of divine protection, inflated claims of power, blindness to God's favor, and failure to give thanks; this signals decline.
TUSTARI:28:78/r4.anchor: وخسف الأشرار هو منع العصمة، والرد إلى الحول والقوة بإطلاق اللسان في الدعاوي العريضة،

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r1.claim: With a circumstantial waw followed by an imperfect verb, the verb must be predicated on an expressed subject, as in رأيته وهو يكتب; without it, the construction fails to convey the state.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r1.anchor: فإذا كان الفعل فيما بعد هذه الواو التي يراد بها الحال مضارعا لم يصلح إلا مبنيا على اسم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r2.claim: Qur'anic circumstantial clauses use the noun-plus-verb form to preserve the intended scene; replacing it with a bare coordinated verb makes the wording and meaning lose their proper shape.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r2.anchor: لوجد اللفظ قد نبا عن المعنى ، والمعنى قد زال عن صورته والحال التي ينبغي أن يكون عليها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r3.claim: Fronting أنت in أنت لا تحسن هذا makes the denial of skill stronger and addresses someone especially confident in his own ability.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r3.anchor: كان أشد لنفي إحسان ذلك عنه من أن تقول : لا تحسن هذا . ويكون الكلام في الأول مع من هو أشد إعجابا بنفسه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r4.claim: The construction والذين هم بربهم لا يشركون emphatically denies associating partners, more strongly than alternatives that omit or reposition هم.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r4.anchor: يفيد من التأكيد في نفي الإشراك عنهم ما لو قيل : والذين لا يشركون بربهم ، أو بربهم لا يشركون ؛ لم يفد ذلك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r5.claim: Other Qur'anic examples repeat the same emphatic pattern: a subject pronoun followed by a negative predicate, including statements that they do not believe or question one another.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p115/r5.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون ﴾ ) وقوله تعالى : ( ﴿ فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p453/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p453/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p453/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba reads Qarun's claim 'on knowledge I have' as meaning 'because of my merit'; another report says he was Israel's most learned person in Torah.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p453/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : معناه لفضل عندي .

FARRA:v2p311/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p311/r5.claim: Qarun claims he received the wealth because he possessed merit and knowledge that made him deserving of it.
FARRA:v2p311/r5.anchor: على فضل عندي، أي كنت أهله ومستحقا له

FARRA:v2p311/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p311/r6.claim: Another construal takes ʿindī as “that is how I see it,” linking Qarun's wording to 39:49.
FARRA:v2p311/r6.anchor: ويقال: (أوتيته على علم) ثم قال (عندي) أي كذاك أرى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r1.claim: Qārūn means that he received his wealth because of merit or distinction he possessed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r1.anchor: {قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} أي لفضل عندي.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r2.claim: Exegetical reports say Qārūn was the most learned of the Israelites in the Torah.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r2.anchor: وروي في التفسير: أنه كان أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة (4) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the criminals enter Hell without being questioned or reckoned.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة (5) يدخلون النار بغير حساب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r4.speaker: غيره
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation says the criminals are recognized by their marks.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r1.claim: The author discusses poetic rhyme defects, including raising one rhyme vowel and lowering another, and repeating the same rhyme twice.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r1.anchor: وخالف في الإكفاء بأن رفع قافية وخفض أخرى. وخالف في الإبطاء بأن أعاد قافية مرتين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r2.speaker: ابن الرقاع
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r2.claim: Ibn al-Riqāʿ describes revising a poem by collecting it, correcting its crookedness and sanad, and straightening it like a lance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الرقاع يذكر تنقيحه شعره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma describes a rare poem whose rhymes avoid sanad and muḥāl.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r3.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة : وشعر قد أرقت له غريب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda defines iqwāʾ as raising one rhyme vowel and lowering another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r4.anchor: هذا قول أبي عبيدة. وبعضهم يجعل الإقواء رفع قافية وجر أخرى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r5.claim: Another definition of iqwāʾ is raising one rhyme ending and making another genitive.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وبعضهم يجعل الإقواء رفع قافية وجر أخرى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers Abu ʿUbayda's account because iqwāʾ derives from quwwa, a strand of rope; losing a metrical part is like losing a strand.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r6.anchor: وقول أبي عبيدة أجود عندي لأن الإقواء من القوة، والقوة: طاقة من الحبل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r7.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r7.claim: The cited line “when she saw the colostrum milk drunk” exemplifies a missing element in the verse; “مشروبة” would make it regular.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r8.claim: Qur'anic Arabic uses many rhetorical modes, including metaphor, analogy, inversion, fronting, ellipsis, repetition, concealment, explicitness, allusion, and shifts in number and address.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r8.anchor: وللعرب المجازات في الكلام، ومعناها: طرق القول ومآخذه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r9.claim: Because Qur'anic expression uses the full range of Arabic figurative speech, no translator can transfer it into another language as the earlier scriptural books were translated.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p21/r9.anchor: وبكل هذه المذاهب نزل القرآن ولذلك لا يقدر أحد من التراجم على أن ينقله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r3.claim: The statement that criminals are not asked about their sins in the Qarun passage expresses the same stage-specific point.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r3.anchor: ومثله: ولا يسئل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

NAHHAS:v3p242/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p242/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives two senses: Qārūn claims the wealth on the basis of merit he possesses, or of knowledge as he understands it.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r13.anchor: تأوله الفراء على معنيين أحدهما على فضل عندي والآخر على علم فيما رأى

NAHHAS:v3p242/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p242/r14.claim: Abū Isḥāq understands Qārūn to mean he acquired the wealth through knowledge of the Torah, which he knew.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r14.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق المعنى إنما أوتيته على علم بالتوراة لأنه كان عالما بها

NAHHAS:v3p242/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r15.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p242/r15.claim: Abū Isḥāq rejects the claim that Qārūn practiced alchemy, since alchemy is false and has no reality.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r15.anchor: وأنكر قول من قال إنه كان يعمل الكيمياء قال لأن الكيمياء باطل لا حقيقة له

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r1.claim: على علم is circumstantial to the subject of أوتيته.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r1.anchor: قوله: { على علم }: حال من مرفوع " أوتيته ".

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r2.claim: عندي is an adverb of أوتيته or an adjective of العلم.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r2.anchor: إما ظرف ل " أوتيته " ، وإما صفة للعلم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r3.claim: من is relative or indefinite-qualified, and is object of أهلك.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r3.anchor: قوله: { من هو أشد }: " من " موصولة أو نكرة موصوفة. وهو في موضع المفعول ب " أهلك ".

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r4.anchor: المفعول ب " أهلك ". و " من قبله " متعلق به.

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r5.claim: من القرون depends on أهلك or is circumstantial to من هو أشد.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r5.anchor: يجوز فيه ذلك، ويجوز أن يكون حالا من " من هو أشد ".

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r6.claim: The common reading is passive, third person, with المجرمون nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r6.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة على البناء للمفعول، وبالياء من تحت ورفع الفعل.

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r7.claim: Abu Ja'far reads ولا تسأل with ت and jussive mood.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر " ولا تسأل " بالتاء من فوق والجزم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r8.speaker: ابن سيرين وأبو العالية
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r8.claim: Ibn Sirin and Abu al-Aliya use ت and jussive mood but make the verb active.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r8.anchor: وابن سيرين وأبو العالية كذلك، إلا أنه مبني للفاعل وهو المخاطب.

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r9.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r9.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq says the active reading requires المجرمين accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r9.anchor: قال ابن أبي إسحاق: " لا يجوز ذلك حتى تنصب المجرمين ".

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r10.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r10.claim: The author of al-Lawami calls the accusative apparent and gives two analyses if nominative is retained.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r10.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح: " هذا هو الظاهر؛ إلا أنه لم يبلغني فيه شيء. فإن تركاه مرفوعا فيحتمل وجهين،

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r11.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r11.claim: Because ذنوبهم is a verbal noun annexed to its agent, المجرمون can follow its underlying case; cf. بعوضة in 2:26.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r11.anchor: لأنهما مرفوعا المحل " يعني أن ذنوبا مصدر مضاف لفاعله. قال: " فحمل المجرمون على الأصل، كما تقدم لنا في قراءة { مثلا ما بعوضة } [البقرة: 26]

SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r12.claim: Al-Samin calls that explanation strained and says the reading should have المجرمين accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:28:78/r12.anchor: وهذا تعسف كثير. ولا ينبغي أن يقرأ ابن سيرين وأبو العالية إلا " المجرمين " بالياء فقط

ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n88/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n88/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n88/r1.claim: Qarun claims his wealth came from his own experience, shrewdness, and ability.
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n88/r1.anchor: as a result of my own experience, shrewdness and ability

ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n89/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n89/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n89/r1.claim: Sinners are generally blind to their failings and consequently do not respond to admonition.
ASAD-NOTES:28:78#n89/r1.anchor: are, as a rule, blind to their own failings and, therefore, not responsive to admonition

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r1.claim: Qārūn attributes his wealth to his own planning and acumen, denies any link to God, and therefore feels no obligation or fear and dismisses the advice he receives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r1.anchor: he did not owe Him an obligation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r2.claim: God comments that Qarun should have remembered that many earlier peoples stronger than him had been destroyed; Pharaoh's recent drowning was a warning he should have heard about.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r2.anchor: but God had destroyed them in the blink of an eye.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r3.claim: Strength here includes means and resources, majesty and grandeur, and weapons and instruments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r3.anchor: the might of people viz a viz means and resources, majesty and grandeur, weapons and instruments

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r4.claim: The word jamʿ refers to the number of people in a family or tribe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r4.anchor: refers to the number of people in a family or tribe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r5.claim: When God seizes criminals, they receive no respite for questioning about their crime or possible pretext; punishment comes immediately.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r5.anchor: they are not given even this much respite that they be asked about their crime and about any pretext they may be having.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r6.claim: At Judgement God will not need to investigate wrongdoers because their limbs will testify against them, as also described in Sūrah al-Raḥmān.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p572/r6.anchor: The forehead, hands, feet and his other limbs will bear wit ness against him.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.claim: Of twelve disputed possessive yāʾs, Nafi opens all except معي ردءا, which he leaves quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا قوله ﴿ معي ردءا ﴾ فإنه أسكنها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr open nine listed possessive yāʾs and leave quiescent إني أريد, ستجدني إن شاء الله, and معي ردءا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير تسع آيات منهن وأسكن ﴿ إني أريد ﴾ و ﴿ ستجدني إن شاء الله ﴾

NASHR:v2p164/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r1.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p164/r1.claim: In the yāʾ-addition set at issue, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar open the yāʾ; the other readers make it still.
NASHR:v2p164/r1.anchor: ففتح الياء منهن نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر

NASHR:v2p164/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p164/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar, and Abū ʿAmr open عندي; Ibn Kathīr’s transmissions vary, with most Maghribi and Egyptian routes opening it but most Iraqi routes dividing between his transmitters.
NASHR:v2p164/r12.anchor: واتفق نافع وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو أيضا على فتح عندي، أولم في القصص

NASHR:v2p342/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r10.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p342/r10.claim: The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr open عندي; Ibn Kathīr’s reading varies by route, as described in the preceding account.
NASHR:v2p342/r10.anchor: عندي أولم يفتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو، واختلف ابن كثير

QIRAAT-ER:28:78:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:78:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:78:6#1/r1.claim: Fatḥa on the final yāʾ gives ʿindiya rather than ʿindī; it is a dialectal pronunciation difference with no meaning change.
QIRAAT-ER:28:78:6#1/r1.anchor: Variant with fatḥa on final yāʾ (ʿindiya instead of ʿindī) — a phonological variation

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p94/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p94/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p94/r1.claim: Qatāda says the criminals enter the Fire without reckoning.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p94/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون ﴾ قال يدخلون النار بغير حساب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r1.claim: Qarun replies to those who advised him, claiming the wealth was given to him on the basis of knowledge he possessed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r1.anchor: مجيبا لمن نصحه ( إنما أوتيته على علم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r2.claim: His reply rejects the implication that God bestowed the wealth without any cause or prior merit on Qarun's part, and asserts that he deserves it because of his knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r2.anchor: كأنه يريد الرد على قولهم : كما أحسن الله اليك لإنبائه عن أنه تعالى أنعم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r3.claim: Most grammarians take على علم as a circumstantial phrase qualifying the passive verb's subject and specifying the cause of the gift and Qarun's claimed entitlement.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r3.anchor: عند أكثر المعربين في موضع الحال من مرفوع أوتيته قيد به العامل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r4.claim: Another grammatical analysis makes على causal and attaches the phrase to أوتيت: he was given the wealth because of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r4.anchor: وجوز كون على تعليلية والجار والمجرور متعلق بأوتيت على أنه ظرف لغو

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r5.claim: On one analysis, عندي modifies علم and means knowledge particular to Qarun rather than his advisers.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r5.anchor: في موضع الصفة لعلم والمراد لعلم مختص بي دونكم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r6.claim: Alternatively, عندي attaches to أوتيت and means in my opinion or judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r6.anchor: وجوز كونه متعلقا بأوتيت ومعناه في ظني ورأيي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r7.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats عندي meaning in my opinion as the predicate of an omitted subject, with an independent sentence affirming Qarun's settled view.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r7.anchor: وفي الكشاف ما هو ظاهر في أن عندي إذا كان بمعنى في ظني ورأيي كان خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r8.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r8.claim: Al-Kashf calls that analysis the stronger one: the phrase is an independent sentence reporting a settled opinion.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r8.anchor: في الكشف : وهذا هو الوجه والمراد بهذأ العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r9.claim: One view identifies Qarun's knowledge as knowledge of the Torah, in which he was the most learned Israelite.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r9.anchor: قيل علم التوراة فانه كان أعلم بني اسرائيل بها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r10.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r10.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani identifies the knowledge as commerce and the ways of earning.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r10.anchor: أبو سليمان الداراني : علم التجارة ووجوه المكاسب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r11.speaker: ابن المسيب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r11.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says it was alchemy: Moses taught one third each to Yusha, Kalib, and Qarun; Qarun tricked the other two and combined their knowledge with his, turning lead and copper into gold.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r11.anchor: ابن المسيب : علم الكيمياء وكان موسى عليه السلام يعلم ذلك فأفاد يوشع بن نون ثلثه وكالب بن يوفا ثلثه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r12.claim: Another account says God taught alchemy to Moses, Moses taught his sister, and she taught Qarun.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r12.anchor: علم الله تعالى موسى عليه السلام علم الكيمياء فعلمه موسى اخته فعلمته أخته قارون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to specify knowledge of the craft of goldworking.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r13.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس تخصيصه بعلم صنعة الذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r14.claim: Another interpretation is knowledge of extracting buried treasure.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r15.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r15.claim: Abu Zayd says the knowledge is God's knowledge: Qarun was given wealth through divine knowledge and a special selection from God; عندي means in his judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r15.anchor: وعن أبي زيد أن المراد بالعلم علم الله تعالى وأن المعنى أوتيته على علم من الله تعالى وتخصيص من لدنه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r16.claim: Another view takes علم to mean the thing known, comparing the phrase with the Qur'anic expression that none encompasses anything of God's knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r16.anchor: وقيل : العلم بمعنى المعلوم كثله في قوله تعالى : ( ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r17.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r17.claim: Muqatil glosses Qarun's claim as receiving wealth because of good that God knew to be in him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r17.anchor: ما روي عن مقاتل أنه قال أي على خير علمه الله تعالى عندي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r18.claim: Interpreting the knowledge as alchemy was common among alchemists, and al-Majmaʿ al-Bayan also attributes that interpretation to al-Kalbi.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r18.anchor: وتفسيره بعلم الكيمياء شائع فيما بين أهلها وفي مجمع البيان حكايته عن الكلبي أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r19.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r19.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the alchemy interpretation because alchemy is false and has no reality.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r19.anchor: الزجاج وقال : إنه لا يصح لأن علم الكيمياء باطل لا حقيقة له

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r20.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r20.claim: Al-Tibi counters that alchemy might have been a miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r20.anchor: وتعقبه الطيبي بأنه لعله كان من قبيل المعجز

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r21.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Tibi's response: if alchemy were a miracle, Qarun could not have possessed it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r21.anchor: وتعقب بأنه ليس بسديد وإلا لما تمكن قارون منه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r22.claim: The word الكيمياء may be Greek, meaning artifice or trick.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r22.anchor: وإنكار الكيمياء وهو لفظ يوناني معناه الحيلة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r23.claim: Another proposed etymology derives الكيمياء from Hebrew كيم يه, meaning that it is from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r23.anchor: أو عبراني وأصله كيم يه بمعنى أنه من الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r24.claim: A third proposed etymology derives the word from Persian كي ميا, glossed as when by a particular method.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r24.anchor: أو فارسي وأصله كي ميا بمعنى متى بطريق مخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r25.speaker: جماعة أجلّة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p113/r25.claim: Al-Alusi says the debate is not unique to al-Zajjaj: some scholars denied alchemy, while others took the opposite position.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r1.claim: The philosophers' debate over Qarun's alleged knowledge turns on whether the seven metals are distinct species or one species differentiated only by properties.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r1.anchor: مبني الكلام في هذه الصناعة عند الحكماء على حال المعادن السبعة النطرقة وهي الذهب والفضة والرصاص

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r2.speaker: الفارابي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r2.claim: Al-Farabi, followed by Andalusian philosophers, holds that the metals are one species differing in qualities such as moisture, dryness, softness, hardness, and color; changing those qualities makes transmutation possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r2.anchor: ذهب اليه المعلم أبو نصر الفارابي وتابعه عليه حكماء الاندلس أنها نوع واحد وان اختلافها بالكيفيات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r3.speaker: ابن باجة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r3.claim: Ibn Bajja transmits Farabi's account of Aristotle: alchemy is possible but very difficult, because same-species metals can transform through changes in their accidents; essential accidents make the process harder, though gold and silver may differ only slightly.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r3.anchor: أبو بكر بن الصائغ المعروف بابن باجة في بعض تصانيفه عن المعلم المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r4.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r4.claim: Ibn Sina and eastern philosophers hold that metals are distinct species by their forms, so craft cannot transmute them because only God creates species forms; Ibn Khaldun reports this position.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114/r4.anchor: والذي ذهب اليه الشيخ أبو علي بن سينا وتابعه عليه حكماء المشرق أنها مختلفة بالفصول وأنها أنواع متباينة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r1.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r1.claim: Ibn Sina allows coloring copper to resemble silver, silver to resemble gold, and removing much of lead's deficiency, but doubts that a species-defining form can be removed or imparted.
