ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r1.anchor: الشيخ سلم امكان أن يصبغ النحاس بصبغ الفضة والفضة بصبغ الذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r2.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi says Ibn Sina's doubt is unresolved because the visible traits separating metals may be accidents rather than species forms, while an unknown form seems impossible to target deliberately.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r2.anchor: فلم يظهر لي امكانه بعد إذ هذه الأمور المحسوسة تشبه أن لا تكون الفصول التي بها تصير هذه الأجساد أنواعا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r3.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r3.claim: Al-Tughra'i answers that alchemy prepares matter to receive a property created by God, rather than manufacturing a species form; analogies include polished bodies receiving light and animals generated from unusual materials.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r3.anchor: وغلطه الطغرائي وهو من أكابر أهل هذه الصناعة وله فيها عدة كتب ورد عليه بأن التدبير والعلاج ليس في تخليق الفصل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi judges al-Tughra'i's answer sound: craft treats matter and prepares it to accept a form, so the artisan need not comprehend or create the form itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r4.anchor: فنحن نحاول مثل ذلك في الذهب والفضة فنتخذ مادة نصفها للتدبير بعد أن يكون فيها استعداد أول

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi argues by analogy with antidotes that either specific effects arise from a mixture rather than a distinct form, or knowledge of a form's effects suffices to create and destroy it; the same reasoning applies to gold.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r5.anchor: وقال الامام بعد ذكره ما سمعت من كلام الشيخ : هو ليس بقوي لأنا نشاهد من الترياق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r6.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r6.claim: Even if a gold form exists, one can identify compatible and incompatible qualities: heating destroys water's form and cooling air acquires it, so analogous treatment can alter gold's defining traits.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p114#2/r6.anchor: ونعلم أن العرض الغير الملائم إذا اشتد في المادة بطلت الصورة مثل الصورة المائية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r1.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r1.claim: First, nature uses unknown elements, proportions, qualities, and durations; humans cannot manufacture metals without knowing these particulars.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r1.anchor: أولها أن الطبيعة إنما تعمل هذه الأجساد من عناصر مجهولة عندنا ولتلك العناصر مقادير معينة مجهولة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r2.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r2.claim: Al-Razi answers the first objection by noting that medicine also works despite comparable ignorance of nature's particulars.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r2.anchor: وأجاب الامام عن الأول بأنه منقوض بصناعة الطب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r3.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r3.claim: Second, a dyeing agent and the metal being dyed cannot be ordered consistently by resistance to fire; equal resistance would make them the same kind and leave their roles reversible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r3.anchor: ثانيها : أن الجوهر الصابغ أما أن يكون أصبر على النار من المصبوغ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r4.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r4.claim: Al-Razi replies that sharing resistance to fire does not imply identity of essence; distinct things can share a property.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r4.anchor: وعن الثاني بأنه لا يلزم من استواء الصابغ والمصبوغ في الصبر على النار استواؤهما في الماهية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r5.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r5.claim: Third, if craft could reproduce what nature makes, nature should also make artifacts such as swords and chairs; since that consequence is false, alchemy by craft is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r5.anchor: ثالثها : أنه لو كان بالصناعة مثلا لما كان بالطبيعة لكن التالي باطل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r6.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r6.claim: Al-Razi cites artificial fire, ammonium chloride made from barley, and various salts as crafted analogues of natural products; lacking an example does not prove impossibility, and the reverse inference from art to nature does not follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r6.anchor: النار الحاصلة بالقدح والنوشادر قد يتخذ من الشعير وكذلك كثير من الزاجات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r7.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r7.claim: Fourth, metals have natural mines as their places of generation, so producing them elsewhere seems as unlikely as animals developing outside wombs.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r7.anchor: هي معادنها وهي لها بمنزلة الارحام للحيوان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r8.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r8.claim: Al-Razi answers that transforming copper into silver treats an imperfect metal rather than creating it, as a physician heals illness outside the place of birth; the disputed point is whether mine-born products can also be produced by craft.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r8.anchor: من أراد أن يقلب النحاس فضة فهو لا يكون كالمحدث للشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r9.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r9.claim: Ibn Khaldun introduces a separate argument against alchemy after recounting Ibn Sina and al-Tughra'i.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p115/r9.anchor: ابن خلدون بعد أن ذكر كلام ابن سينا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r1.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r1.claim: Ibn Khaldun says alchemists prepare matter and imitate nature's treatment of metals, sometimes doubling active and passive powers to shorten the process; gold takes 1,080 great solar cycles in its mine.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r1.anchor: أنهم بعد الوقوف على المادة المستعدة بالاستعداد الأول يجعلونها موضوعا ويحاذون في تدبيرها وعلاجها تدبير الطبيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r2.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r2.claim: Alternatively, practitioners seek an elixir with a ferment-like form that converts matter into its own nature, as yeast changes dough and helps it become digestible nourishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r2.anchor: أو يتحرون بعلاجهم ذلك حصول صورة مزاجية لتلك المادة تصيرها كالخميرة للخبز

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r3.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r3.claim: Generated elemental mixtures require unequal proportions of the four elements, a dominant part, and innate heat that produces and preserves their form.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r3.anchor: كل متكون من المولدات العنصرية لابد فيه من اجتماع العناصر الاربعة على نسب متفاوتة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r4.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r4.claim: Generation unfolds through stages whose proportions, qualities, and innate heat change; an alchemist would have to follow gold's long sequence of stages in its mine.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r4.anchor: وانظر شأن الانسان في تطوره نطفة ثم علقة ثم وثم إلى نهايته

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r5.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r5.claim: Because any craft requires prior conception of its outcome, the alchemist must know each stage and ratio of gold and calculate equivalent intensified powers or a ferment-like form.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116/r5.anchor: ومن شرط الصناعة مطلقا تصور ما يقصد إليه بها فمن الأمثال السائرة في ذلك للحكماء أول العمل آخر الفكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r1.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r1.claim: Ibn Khaldun argues that only God's encompassing knowledge can grasp every mineral condition; human knowledge is too limited, making alchemy comparable to creating a person from semen and, in his view, impossible for that reason rather than because forms cannot change.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r1.anchor: وهذه كلها إنما يحصرها العلم المحيط وهو علمه عز وجل والعلوم البشرية قاصرة عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r2.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r2.claim: He adds that God's wisdom makes gold and silver rare as the foundation of people's earnings and stored wealth; craft production would make them common and defeat that purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r2.anchor: حكمة الله تعالى في الحجرين وندرتهما أنهما عمدتا مكاسب الناس ومتمولاتهم فلو حصل عليها بالصنعة لبطلت حكمة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r3.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r3.claim: He also argues that nature would not take a longer path if the claimed artificial process were a valid, quicker route to gold and silver.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r3.anchor: الطبيعة لا تترك اقرب الطرق في أفعالها وترتكب الأبعد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r4.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r4.claim: Ibn Khaldun accepts al-Tughra'i's examples of animals generated from unusual materials, but says no scholar has reliably found alchemy or its method; practitioners' confused claims would have been preserved and verified if true.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r4.anchor: وأما تشبيه الطغرائي هذا التدبير بما عثر عليه من مفردات لأمثاله في الطبيعة كالعقرب والحية وتخليقهما فأمر صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r5.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r5.claim: He says no alchemy practitioner has produced a dependable account or reproducible method, and that their claims remain false stories rather than transmitted knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p116#2/r5.anchor: وأما الكيمياء فلم ينقل عن أحد من أهل العلم أنه عثر عليها ولا على طريقها وما زال منتحلوها يخبطون فيها خبط عشواء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r1.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r1.claim: Ibn Khaldun rejects the yeast analogy: yeast corrupts and prepares dough for digestion, an easy process, whereas the elixir must elevate metal to something nobler, and generation is harder than corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r1.anchor: إن الخميرة إنما تقلب العجين وتعده للهضم وهو فساد والفساد في المواد سهل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r2.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r2.claim: He says that if alchemy exists, it is not a natural craft but an extraordinary psychic or supernatural effect like walking on water or creating birds, and thus belongs to miracle, saintly wonder, or magic; he cites al-Majriti and Jabir as treating it this way.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r2.anchor: إن الكيمياء إن صح وجودها كما يزعم الحكماء المتكلمون فيها فليس من باب الصنائع الطبيعية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r3.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r3.claim: Al-Razi argues that alchemy is possible because the seven metals share being molten, fire-resistant, and malleable; gold differs by yellowness and heaviness, or by a form producing those properties, which copper might acquire.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r3.anchor: وإلى إمكانها ذهب الامام الرازي فقال الحق أمكانها لأن الأجساد السبعة مشتركة في أنها أجساد ذائبة صابرة على النار منطرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r4.claim: Al-Alusi's own conclusion is that alchemy is possible as a natural craft but extremely difficult, known only to those whom God specially enables; its origin is divine revelation, though some acquire it through purification, study, and experiment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117/r4.anchor: والحق أن الكيمياء ممكنة وأنها من الصنائع الطبيعية لكن العلم بها من أقاصي العلوم الصعبة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r1.speaker: ارس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r1.claim: Ars, a leading authority on the art, says it first came by revelation from God, then disappeared before being recovered from books.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r1.anchor: ارس : وهو من أجلة أهل هذا العلم كان أوله وحيا من الله تعالى ثم درس وباد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r2.claim: The source says those who discover alchemy usually keep it secret except from those God chooses; sages agreed to conceal it from the unworthy, and a saying attributes this secrecy to an innate divine covenant on human minds.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r2.anchor: وقد جرت سنة الله تعالى فيمن ظفر به بكتمه إلا على من شاء الله تعالى وتواصت الحكماء على كتمه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r3.speaker: جابر بن حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r3.claim: Jabir says sages encoded alchemy in obscure terms and symbols: experts can unlock them, while the ignorant may test the materials without success and blame the sages for concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r3.anchor: وقد نص جابر بن حيان وهو أمام في هذه الصنعة وإنكار أنه كان موجودا حمق في كتابه سر الاسرار على ما قلنا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r4.speaker: جابر بن حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r4.claim: Jabir says secrecy protects the world's economic order: if everyone knew the secret, people would lose the incentives of reward and fear, work would cease, and society would be ruined.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r4.anchor: وإن الناس الصناع والمقاتلة لا يعملون إلا لرغبة أو رهبة فعلموا أنهم إن أفشوا هذا السر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi rejects Ibn Khaldun's argument from human inability to comprehend all processes: if alchemy came through revelation, that limitation does not establish its impossibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r5.anchor: أن من الاستحالة لعدم الاحاطة إذا ثبت أنها كانت عن وحي ليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi also rejects the claim that nature never takes the shorter route: nature can have both a longer common path and a shorter rare path, which God enables some servants to use.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r6.anchor: ومثل ذلك ما ذكره من أن الطبيعة لا تترك أقرب الطرق في أفعالها وترتكب الأبعد لأنا نقول

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says the renowned historical masters of alchemy did not merely blunder; their riddling language reflects intentional concealment, while Ibn Khaldun's criticism may fit most contemporary pretenders but does not disprove possibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r7.anchor: إن أراد بهم أئمة هذه الصناعة كهرمس وسقراط وإفلاطون واغاريمون وفيثاغورس وهرقل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi notes that al-Tughra'i condemned the pretenders and confused practitioners of his own age in his book Tarkib al-Anwar.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p117#2/r8.anchor: وقد ذم الطغرائي هذا الصنف من الناس في كتابه تراكيب الأنوار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r1.claim: Alusi says alchemy has nearly disappeared, its seekers are mocked, and its practitioners conceal its methods from one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r1.anchor: المعلم الناصح موجود في كل صنعة إلا في هذا الفن

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r2.claim: He divides current practitioners into swindlers who profit through ignorant experiments and dupes misled by greed, false hopes, and neglect of honest work.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r2.anchor: بين مخادع يبيع دينه ومروءته بعرض من الدنيا قليل ويتلف أموال الناس بالتجارب الصادرة عن الجهل وبين مخدوع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r3.claim: Most readers of Jabir and similar authors are deceived by literal claims; the old masters warn that their books are symbolic riddles whose surface should not be trusted.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r3.anchor: يأخذ بظواهر كلامهم ويغتر بجلايا دعاويهم دون حقائق معانيهم وهم وجميع من مضى من حكماء هذه الصنعة يحذرون الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r4.claim: Alchemy works through ordinary causes hidden from most people, not through psychic influence or supernatural action, magic, or sorcery.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r4.anchor: هي بأسباب عادية لكنها خفية على أكثر الناس لا دخل لتأثير النفوس فيها أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r5.claim: A prophet or saint who produces an alchemical result without using those causes would perform a miracle or wonder.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r5.anchor: قد يكون من النبي أو الولي ما يكون من الكيماوي من غير معاطاة تلك الاسباب فيكون ذا كرامة أو معجزة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r6.claim: Alchemical authors' magical-sounding style does not make the art sorcery; they deliberately encode it through planetary schemes, parables, and fable-like stories.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r6.anchor: كون منحى كلام بعض الحكماء فيها منحى كلامهم في الأمور السحرية لا يدل على أنها من أنواع السحر أو توابعه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r7.claim: Only a few know the craft, so trying to master it from books without a wise reader of its symbols is sheer madness.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r7.anchor: من غير حكيم عارف برموزها كما يفعله جهلة المنتحلين لها اليوم محض جنون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r8.claim: Alusi thinks alchemy probably originated in divine revelation or something similar, citing material collected by al-Tughra'i.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r8.anchor: وكون أصلها الوحي الالهي أو نحو ذلك هو الذي يغلب على الظن وقد أورد الطغرائي في كتبه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r9.speaker: هرمس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r9.claim: Al-Tughra'i quotes Hermes saying God revealed to Seth to plant gold in pure white earth and water it with the water of life.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r9.anchor: أوحى إلى شيت بن آدم عليهما السلام أن ازرع الذهب في الأرض البيضاء النقية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r10.speaker: مارية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r10.claim: Marya says she speaks by God's command to Moses, who was taught that the stone called nistaris holds the dye.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r10.anchor: وقالت مارية : إني لست أقول لكم من تلقاء نفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r11.speaker: ذو سيموس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r11.claim: Al-Tughra'i's material attributes this art to Moses through Dhu Simus.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r11.anchor: وقال بنسبتها إلى موسى عليه السلام ذو سيموس وارس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r12.speaker: ارس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r12.claim: Aris says the Jews in Egypt practiced the art; Joseph, the first Israelite to enter Egypt, knew it and Pharaoh honored his God-given wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r12.anchor: وذكر ارس أن العمل بها كان طوع اليهود بمصر وكان يوسف عليه السلام وهو أول من دخل مصر من بني إسرائيل يعرف ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r13.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r13.claim: Al-Tughra'i also cites an encoded passage attributing alchemy to Solomon.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r13.anchor: وذكر أيضا فصلا مرموزا فيه نسبه إلى سليمان عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r14.speaker: الطرسوسي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r14.claim: Al-Tarsusi says Adam received knowledge of everything, including this craft, which passed from people to people until Hermes the First.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r14.anchor: إن الله تعالى لما أهبط آدم عليه السلام من الجنة عوضه علم كل شيء وكان علم الصنعة مما علمه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r15.claim: Al-Tarsusi cites a connected report from al-Tabari that the Prophet said the earth was shown to him and he was given white and red sulfur; Alusi gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p118/r15.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : زويت لي الأرض فأريت مشارقها ومغاربها وأعطيت

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r1.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r1.claim: Jabir transmitted many reports about alchemy from Ja'far al-Sadiq and attributed several books to him; Alusi neither verifies nor denies them and deems Ja'far too eminent to fabricate.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r1.anchor: وروى جابر عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه في ذلك روايات كثيرة حتى أنه أسند اليه عدة من كتبه ولا أحقق قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r2.claim: A report has Ali call alchemy prophecy's sister and manliness' twin, describe its hidden elements and their combination into latent gold, and explain that he withholds its teaching because of the soul's evil prompting.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r2.anchor: علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه سئل فقيل : له ما تقول فيما خاض الناس فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r3.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r3.claim: Al-Tughra'i says about sixty prophets and sages affirmed alchemy's truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r3.anchor: وذكر في كتابه مفاتيح الرحمة ومصابيح الحكمة عن ستين نبيا وحكيما أنهم قالوا بحقية هذا العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r4.claim: Alusi doubts these traditions: if hadith experts had accepted a report affirming alchemy, it would have become widely known, and major scholars would not have rejected it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r4.anchor: والأغلب على الظن أنه لو كان في الكيمياء خبر مقبول عند المحدثين لشاع ولما أنكرها من هو من أجلتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r5.speaker: ابن تيمية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r5.claim: Alusi notes that Ibn Taymiyya denied alchemy's established authenticity and wrote a treatise rejecting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r5.anchor: كشيخ الاسلام تقي الدين أحمد بن تيمية فانه ينكر ثبوتها وألف رسالة في إنكارها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r6.claim: Alusi qualifies al-Safadi's claim that Najm al-Din al-Baghdadi refuted alchemy: the rebuttal may concern rational arguments, while Najm was unmatched in transmitted learning but weaker in rational inquiry.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r6.anchor: ولعل رد الشيخ نجم الدين ابن أبي الذر البغدادي وتزييفه ما قاله فيها كما زعم الصفدي إنما كان فيما هو من باب الاستدلالات العقلية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r7.claim: Even highly regarded scholars have vacillated, sometimes denying and sometimes affirming alchemy.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r7.anchor: حتى أن بعض من تعقد عليه الخناصر اضطرب في أمرها فأنكرها تارة وأقر بها أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r8.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r8.claim: Alusi says Ibn Sina was reported both to affirm alchemy initially and later to recant, yet never to have learned its actual method; al-Tughra'i mocks his treatise as embarrassing and unprincipled.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p119/r8.anchor: فهذا شيخ الحكماء ورئيسهم أبو علي بن سينا سمعت منقل عنه اولا وحكي عنه الرجوع عنه وعلى جودة ذهنه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r1.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r1.claim: Al-Tughra'i says Ibn Sina's ardor and intuition that alchemy was real led him to write on it; he handled physical principles well but the hidden method remained inaccessible to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r1.anchor: إن الشيخ أبا علي بن سينا لفرط شغفه بهذا العلم وحدسه القوي بأنه حق صنف رسالة فيه فأحسن فيما يتعلق باصول الطبيعيات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r2.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r2.claim: Al-Tughra'i faults Ibn Sina for omitting accurate procedures, the proper mixture and weights, secret combinations, fire stages, and the indispensable tool among ten conditions.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r2.anchor: لم يذكر في التدابير المختصة بعلمنا لفظة صحيحة ولا أشار إلى ذكر المزاج الحق والأوزان والتراكيب المكتومة والنيران وطبقاتها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r3.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r3.claim: Al-Tughra'i says Ibn Sina resorted only to common recipes involving quicksilver, sulfur, and horse dung, and should have avoided a field he did not know.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r3.anchor: ولم يتجاوز من عند الحشوية من تدابير الزوابق والكباريت والدفن في زبل الخيل والتشاغل بهذه القاذورات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r4.speaker: الطغرائي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r4.claim: Al-Tughra'i says witnesses to Ibn Sina's experiments and his handwritten notes drawn from Jabir and Khalid show that he did not know the real art.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r4.anchor: وقد تأدى إلينا من تدابيره عن أصحابه الذين شاهدوها أنه لم يكن يعرف حقيقة علمنا وقد رأينا بخطه من التعاليق الملتقطة من كلام جابر بن حيان وخالد بن يزيد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r5.claim: Taking Qarun's knowledge to mean extracting buried treasures presupposes that alchemy exists; practitioners of letter science and talismans affirm it, though Alusi leaves its truth uncertain.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r5.anchor: القول بأن المراد بالعلم في اة ية علم استخراج الكنوز والدفائن يستدعي ثبوت هذا العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r6.claim: The question rebukes Qarun's boast and warns him that God destroyed earlier people who surpassed him, a lesson he could have learned from scripture, Moses, histories, or storytellers.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r6.anchor: تقرير لعلمه ذلك وتنبيه على خطئه في اغتراره وعلمه بذلك من التوراة أو من موسى عليه السلام أو من كتب التواريخ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r7.claim: Strength may be physical or moral, and their greater gathering may mean wealth or people who surrounded and served them; Qarun should not have been deceived by his own resources.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r7.anchor: والقوة تحتمل القوة الحسية والمعنوية والجمع يحتمل جمع المال وجمع الرجال

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r8.claim: One parsing takes the interrogative as condemning an omitted claim, with the following clause circumstantial; it denies Qarun's claimed knowledge by showing he ignored history's lesson.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r8.anchor: أن تكون الهمزة للانكار داخلة على مقدر وجملة ولم يعلم حالية مقررة للانكار ودالة على انتفاء ما دخلت عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r9.claim: Another parsing coordinates لم يعلم with an omitted clause and denies Qarun knowledge because he failed to act on what he knew.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p120/r9.anchor: ونفي العلم عنه لعدم جريه على موجبه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r1.claim: Alusi takes this as an afterlife scene: the pronoun refers to criminals, and God or angels do not ask them for information because God knows and angels know records or recognize faces.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن هذا في الآخرة وأن ضمير ذنوبهم للمجرمين وفاعل السؤال إما الله تعالى أو الملائكة عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r2.claim: The denial is a question seeking information, as in 55:39; angels can identify sinners by their marks, as in 55:41, while the question in 15:92 is reproach, so the verses do not conflict.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r2.anchor: سؤال الاستعلام ونفي ذلك بالنسبة اليه عز وجل ظاهر وبالنسبة إلى الملائكة عليهم السلام لأنهم مطلعون على صحائفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r3.claim: Alternatively, the negative and affirmative questions can have the same sense but occur at different places or times, since Judgment Day has many stations and is long.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون السؤال في الموضعين بمعنى والنفي والاثبات باعتبار موضعين أو زمانين والمواقف يوم القيامة كثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r4.claim: The sentence is probably outside the scope of Qarun's knowledge claim and extends the threat from worldly destruction to the harsher afterlife; not asking a guilty person signals certain punishment. Al-Zamakhshari calls it a concluding gloss.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r4.anchor: لما هدد قارون بذكر اهلاك من قبله من أضرابه في الدنيا أردف ذلك بما فيه تهديد كافة المجرمين بما هو أشنع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r5.claim: A reported alternative places the statement in this life: God destroyed earlier generations already knowing their sins, so there was no need to question them.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r5.anchor: المراد أنه تعالى أهلك من أهلك من القرون عن علم منه سبحانه بذنوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r6.claim: Another reading makes the pronoun refer to the destroyed generations and construes criminals and noncriminals as not being asked about their sins; Alusi dismisses this and the worldly reading as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r6.anchor: وكلا القولين كما ترى وربما يختلج في دهنك عطف هذه الجملة على جملة الاستفهام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r7.claim: Though one might attach the clause to the question or make it circumstantial to the destroyer or destroyed, Alusi rejects those syntactic connections as unworthy of the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r7.anchor: لكن إذا تأملت أدنى تأمل أخرجته من ذهنك وأبيت حمل كلام الله تعالى الجليل على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r8.claim: Abu Ja'far's transmission reads the verb as second-person jussive and accusative المجرمين.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر في رواية ( ولا تسأل ) بتاء الخطاب والجزم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r9.speaker: أبو العالية وابن سيرين
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliya and Ibn Sirin likewise read ولا تسأل; Alusi is unsure of their case ending, though he thinks accusative is likelier.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية وابن سيرين ( ولا تسأل 9 كذلك ولم ندر أنصبا المجرمين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r10.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r10.claim: The author of al-Lawami permits nominative المجرمون by supplying an omitted predicate, or by treating it as a substitute for the pronoun governed by ذنوب; the latter depends on disputed verbal-noun agreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p121/r10.anchor: الأول أن يكون ضمير ذنوبهم للمهلكين من القرون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r1.claim: Qarūn claims his wealth came from merit and goodness God knew in him, deeming him worthy and favoring him with wealth as with other gifts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r1.anchor: أي: على فضل وخير علمه الله عندي فرآني أهلا لذلك، ففضلني بهذا المال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r2.claim: One view takes the knowledge as alchemy: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab says Moses taught one third each to Joshua, Caleb, and Qarūn; Qarūn tricked the other two into combining their shares, producing his wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: كان موسى يعلم الكيمياء فعلم يوشع بن نون ثلث ذلك العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r3.claim: Another view says Qarūn meant his knowledge of trade, farming, and other kinds of earning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r3.anchor: وقيل: "على علم عندي" بالتصرف في التجارات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r4.claim: God had destroyed earlier unbelieving generations that were stronger and possessed greater wealth and numbers than Qarūn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r4.anchor: الكافرة، {من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا} للأموال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r5.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r5.claim: Qatāda says criminals enter the Fire without reckoning or questioning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: يدخلون النار بغير حساب ولا سؤال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the angels do not ask about them because they recognize the criminals by their marks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني لا يسأل الملائكة عنهم، لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r7.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they are not asked to obtain information; the questioning is for rebuke and reproach.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p222/r7.anchor: قال الحسن: لا يسألون سؤال استعلام وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r7.claim: Qarun claims his knowledge made him superior to others and entitled him to status and wealth; علم is circumstantial and may mean Torah knowledge, in which he excelled.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r7.anchor: فضلت به على الناس واستوجبت به التفوق عليهم بالجاه والمال

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r8.claim: Other proposed meanings of his claimed knowledge are alchemy, trade and estate management, or knowledge of Joseph's treasures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r8.anchor: وقيل هو الكيمياء وقيل علم التجارة والدهقنة وسائر المكاسب

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r9.claim: عندي may describe the knowledge or attach to أوتيته, meaning according to my belief or opinion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r9.anchor: صفة له أو متعلق ب { أوتيته } كقولك: جاز هذا عندي

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r10.claim: The question rebukes Qarun for boasting in strength and wealth despite knowing that stronger and richer past nations were destroyed; he had read or heard their histories.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r10.anchor: تعجب وتوبيخ على اغتراره بقوته وكثرة ماله مع علمه بذلك لأنه قرأه في التوراة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r11.claim: Alternatively, the question rebuts his claim to knowledge: did he lack the knowledge of history that could have protected him from their fate?
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r11.anchor: أو رد لادعائه للعلم وتعظمه به بنفي هذا العلم عنه أي أعنده مثل ذلك العلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r12.claim: The criminals are not asked to supply information because God knows their sins, or to be rebuked because punishment comes suddenly; God knows and will punish all sinners.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r12.anchor: سؤال استعلام فإنه تعالى مطلع عليها أو معاتبة فإنهم يعذبون بها بغتة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.claim: After the partners’ helplessness in the Hereafter, the text shows God’s rule in this world by destroying arrogant people who cannot save one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.anchor: ولما دل على عجزهم في تلك الدار , وعلمهم أن المتصرف في جميع الأقدار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r5.claim: Qarun claims the wealth came through knowledge he possessed, making him its deserving cause rather than indebted to anyone.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r5.anchor: فأنا مستحق لذلك , وذلك العلم هو السبب في حصوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r6.claim: One unattributed view identifies Qarun's knowledge as alchemy.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r6.anchor: وقد قيل : إن ذلك العلم هو الكيمياء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r7.claim: The restrictive إنما in Qarun's statement implies that he credits his own knowledge and denies anyone else a favor in his wealth.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r8.claim: The passive verb suggests that Qarun does not know who gave him the wealth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r8.anchor: وبناء الفعل للمجهول إشارة إلى عدم علمه بالمؤتى من هو

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r9.claim: Qarun should fear that God can strip away his knowledge, wealth, and life; he had no true agency in receiving them, and God can remove them as He bestowed them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r9.anchor: لا صنع له في الحقيقة في ذلك أصلا , لأن الله قد أفقر من هو أجل منه حيلة وأكثر علما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r10.claim: The rebuke points to God's prior destruction of generations stronger in body, knowledge, supporters, and servants, and richer in wealth and people; Pharaoh was among them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r10.anchor: من هو أشد منه } أي قرون { قوة } أي في البدن , والمعاني من العلم وغيره , والأنصار والخدم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r11.claim: Including من قبله limits the reference to preceding generations; without من, the description would encompass all earlier time.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r11.anchor: ولو حذفها لاستغرق الإهلاك على ذلك الوصف جميع ما تقدمه من الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r12.claim: He glosses قرون as generations whose hardness is like that of horns.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r12.anchor: من القرون } أي الذين هم في الصلابة كالقرون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r13.claim: Even Pharaoh, who consulted Qarun about his kingdom and had immense wealth and forces, could not escape destruction for wrongdoing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r13.anchor: ولا امتنع عليه ذلك لعلم عند أحد منهم ولا جمع , بل أخذهم لبغيهم وقبح تقلبهم وسعيهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r1.claim: Human rulers question those they punish because they lack full knowledge and may accept a denial or hidden excuse; God knows inner secrets and needs no such inquiry.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r1.anchor: وأمل المطلع على بواطن الضمائر وخفايا السرائر فغني عن ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r2.claim: Naming the criminals shows that their criminality warrants destruction; جرم is severing what should be joined and joining what should be severed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p519/r2.anchor: أن الموجب للإهلاك الإجرام , وهو قطع ما ينبغي وصله بوصل ما ينبغي قطعه

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r10.claim: Qatada reads Qarun's claim as saying he received the wealth for goodness and knowledge he possessed.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r10.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} يقول على خير عندي وعلم عندي

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r11.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says Qarun meant that God knew he deserved the wealth.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r11.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} يقول: علم الله أني أهل لذلك

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r12.claim: Qatada identifies the criminals who are not questioned as polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r12.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} قال: المشركون

DURR-FULL:v6p440/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r1.claim: Continuing Qatada's explanation, the criminals are neither questioned about their sins nor reckoned with, since they enter Hell without reckoning.
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r1.anchor: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم ولا يحاسبون لدخول النار بغير حساب

DURR-FULL:v6p440/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r2.claim: Mujahid connects this to 55:41: criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes, so angels do not need to question them.
DURR-FULL:v6p440/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون} قال: كقوله {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} الرحمن الآية 41

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r1.claim: Qatada glosses Qarun's claim as receiving the wealth because of goodness and knowledge he possessed.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : انما اوتيته على علم عندي يقول : على خير عندي وعلم عندي .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun meant that God's approval of him and knowledge of his merit were why God gave him the wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r2.anchor: لولا رضا الله عني ومعرفته بفضلي ما اعطاني هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Qarun meant that God knew he was deserving of the wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r3.anchor: عن السدي قال : انما اوتيته على علم عندي علم الله اني اهل لذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the criminals as polytheists: they are punished without being questioned or reckoned for their sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ولا يسال عن ذنوبهم المجرمون يقول : المشركون لا يسالون عن ذنوبهم ، يعذبون ولا يحاسبون .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r5.claim: Al-Rabi says they are not asked to enumerate their sins: their records are given to them, so they do not protest injustice, only the accounting.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس ، قوله : ولا يسال عن ذنوبهم المجرمون قال : لا يسالون عن احصائها يقول : هاتوا فبينوها لنا ، ولكن اعطوها في كتب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the criminals are not questioned about what destroyed earlier peoples or where they ended, so they could learn from them; instead they persist as before.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب ولا يسال عن ذنوبهم المجرمون الذين كانوا قبلهم عما اهلكوا وعن منزلهم فيعتبروا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r7.claim: In another report, Qatada explains that the criminals enter Hell without reckoning.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3012/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : ولا يسال عن ذنوبهم المجرمون قال : يدخلون النار بغير حساب .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3013/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3013/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3013/r1.claim: Mujahid says they are recognized by their marks, including black faces and blue eyes, so the angels do not need to ask about them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3013/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ولا يسال عن ذنوبهم المجرمون قال : كقوله : يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم سود الوجوه زرقا ، الملائكة لا تسال عنهم قد عرفتهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r9.claim: Qarun’s unconnected reply is a self-important answer meant to silence his admonishers after their rebuke challenged his pride.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r9.anchor: جواب عن موعظة واعظيه من قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r10.claim: إنما combines إن with the blocking ما as one particle; its correct spelling joins the nūn to mīm, and it restricts the claim to one cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r10.anchor: و { إنما } هذه هي أداة الحصر المركبة من ( إن ) و ( ما ) الكافة مصيرتين كلمة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r11.claim: Qarun claims that he was given the wealth solely because of knowledge he possesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r11.anchor: والمعنى : ما أوتيت هذا المال إلا على علم علمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r12.claim: The pronoun in أوتيته refers to the relative ما in the admonishers’ earlier phrase فيما آتاك الله; the passive voice leaves the giver understood from their words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r12.anchor: وضمير { أوتيته } عائد إلى ( ما ) الموصولة في قولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r13.claim: على علم is circumstantial, qualifying the nominative pronoun in the passive verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r13.anchor: و { على علم } في موضع الحال من الضمير المرفوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r1.claim: عندي qualifies علم, emphasizing Qarun’s command of the knowledge and his reputation for it; this reading best fits the following rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r1.anchor: وقوله { عندي } صفة ل { علم } تأكيدا لتمكنه من العلم وشهرته به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r2.claim: The author prefers this construction because it coheres with the ensuing reminder that God destroyed earlier generations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r2.anchor: هذا هو الوجه في تفسير هذه الجملة من الآية وهو الذي يستقيم مع قوله تعالى عقبه { أو لم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون } الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r3.claim: Other commentators propose different constructions for على, العلم, and عندي, but the author does not detail them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r3.anchor: وذكر المفسرون وجوها تسفر عن أشكال أخرى من تركيب نظم الآية في محمل معنى { على } ومحمل المراد من ( العلم ) ومحمل { عندي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r4.claim: The discourse now turns to address the Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r4.anchor: وقوله { أو لم يعلم } الآية إقبال على خطاب المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r5.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses emphatic rebuke and astonishment that Qarun failed to heed God’s destruction of people who exulted in blessings and strength, as though he had forgotten what he knew.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r5.anchor: والهمزة في { أو لم يعلم } للاستفهام الإنكاري التعجيبي تعجيبا من عدم جريه على موجب علمه بأن الله أهلك أمما على بطرهم النعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r6.claim: The surprise is that Qarun remembered much knowledge yet let this lesson slip, as the proverb says, one remembered something while forgetting other things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r6.anchor: ونسيانه حتى صار كأنه لم يعلمه تعجيبا من فوات مراعاة ذلك منه مع سعة علمه بغيره من باب ( حفظت شيئا وغابت عنك أشياء )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r7.claim: The interrogative clause is parenthetical between parts of the story, attached to Qarun’s claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r7.anchor: وعطف هذا الاستفهام على جملة { قال إنما أوتيته }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r8.claim: Strength is what enables difficult tasks, by analogy with bodily power for carrying heavy loads; compare 8:60.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r8.anchor: والقوة : ما به يستعان على الأعمال الصعبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r9.claim: جمع means a gathered group of people.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r10.claim: An unnamed view says Qarun’s followers numbered 250 Israelite leaders over groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r10.anchor: قيل : كان أشياع قارون مائتين وخمسين من بني إسرائيل رؤساء جماعات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r11.claim: The closing sentence is an independent summary, not coordinated with God’s destruction of earlier generations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r11.anchor: وجملة { ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون } تذييل للكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r12.claim: The denied questioning is in this world, not the questioning of the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r12.anchor: والسؤال المنفي السؤال في الدنيا وليس سؤال الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r13.claim: One possibility is that questioning figuratively denies any need to inquire: God knows their sins and punishes their crimes; the warning tells criminals to fear sudden seizure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r13.anchor: والمعنى : يحتمل أن يكون السؤال كناية عن عدم الحاجة إلى السؤال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, the question is literal: a criminal is not questioned before punishment because the messengers clarified good and evil and God gave respite; then He may seize them suddenly, as at 6:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون السؤال بمعناه الحقيقي ، أي لا يسأل المجرم عن جرمه قبل عقابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r15.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying God gives an unjust person respite, then seizes him without letting him escape; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p181#2/r15.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إن الله يمهل الظالم حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r1.claim: Qarun answers his people's warning about piety in wealth God favored him with by becoming arrogant, admiring himself, and evading their demand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r1.anchor: القائل قارون لما وعظه قومه وندبوه إلى اتقاء الله تعالى في المال الذي أعطاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r2.claim: The majority say Qarun claimed knowledge that made him deserving of his wealth and favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r2.anchor: فقال الجمهور منهم إنه ادعى أن عنده علما استوجب به أن يكون صاحب ذلك المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r3.claim: Some say he meant Torah knowledge and memorization, which they regard as deceitful display.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r4.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani says Qarun meant experience and techniques for growing wealth, crediting his own discernment and effort.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r4.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداراني: أراد العلم بالتجارب ووجوه تثمير المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r5.speaker: ابن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r5.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says he meant knowledge of alchemy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r5.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: أراد علم الكيمياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r6.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say Qarun claimed God had chosen him and granted the wealth through divine knowledge; “with me” means in his belief or opinion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وغيره: إنما أراد أوتيته على علم من الله وتخصيص من لدنه قصدني به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r7.claim: Either way, the Qur'an exposes Qarun's delusion: God destroyed peoples and kings stronger than him and greater in amassed wealth or retinue.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r7.anchor: وعلى الاحتمالين معا فقد نبه القرآن على خطئه في اغتراره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r8.claim: Earlier peoples exceeded Qarun in power and in wealth or surrounding followers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r8.anchor: من هو أشد من قارون قوة وأكثر جمعا إما للمال وإما للحاشية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r9.claim: “Did he not know?” suggests Qarun boasted of his own knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أولم يعلم يرجح أن قارون تشبع بعلم نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb connects the clause to what precedes: each of the destroyed people is addressed and punished for what pertains to him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r10.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: هو كلام متصل بمعنى ما قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r11.claim: Another group takes this as a fresh statement about the Resurrection: criminals are not questioned about their sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو إخبار مستأنف عن حال يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r12.claim: Qatada says they are not questioned because they enter the Fire without reckoning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r12.anchor: قال قتادة ذلك لأنهم يدخلون النار بغير حساب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r13.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r13.claim: Qatada and Mujahid say angels recognize criminals by darkened, disfigured faces and so do not question them, as in 55:41.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا ومجاهد: معناه أن الملائكة لا تسأل عن ذنوبهم لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.claim: The Qur'an includes verses requiring questioning (37:24) and verses denying that people are asked (55:39).
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.anchor: وفي كتاب الله تعالى آيات تقتضي أن الناس يوم القيامة يسألون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.speaker: الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.claim: Some say the passages concern different stations and groups.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.anchor: فقال الناس في هذا إنها مواطن وطوائف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers that questioning passages mean rebuke and confirmation, while denials mean requests for information; God already knows, and rebuke is not the informational questioning denied.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.anchor: ويشبه عندي أن تكون الآيات التي توجب السؤال إنما يراد بها أسئلة التوبيخ والتقرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ إنما أوتيته ﴾ يعني المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r2.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that Qarun meant knowledge of gold-making.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r2.anchor: أحدها على علم عندي بصنعة الذهب رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects this as unsupported because alchemy is false and unreal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا لا أصل له لأن الكيمياء باطل لا حقيقة له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun meant that God was pleased with him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r4.anchor: والثاني برضى الله عني قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r5.claim: Muqatil says Qarun meant that God knew goodness in him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r5.anchor: والثالث على خير علمه الله عندي قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r6.claim: Al-Farra says Qarun credited his own superior knowledge; al-Zajjaj says he claimed his Torah knowledge earned it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r6.anchor: والرابع إنما أعطيته لفضل علمي قاله الفراء قال الزجاج ادعى أنه أعطي المال لعلمه بالتوراة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits knowledge of ways to earn wealth as another interpretation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r7.anchor: والخامس على علم عندي بوجوه المكاسب حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r8.claim: The person who should have known is Qarun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ أو لم يعلم ﴾ يعني قارون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r9.claim: God destroyed earlier deniers of messengers despite their greater strength and wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r9.anchor: بالعذاب ﴿ من قبله من القرون ﴾ في الدنيا حين كذبوا رسلهم من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا للأموال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says criminals are not questioned to discover their sins, though questioned in rebuke.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r10.anchor: أحدها لا يسألون ليعلم ذلك من قبلهم وإن سئلوا سؤال توبيخ قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r11.claim: Mujahid says angels recognize sinners by their marks and do not need to ask about their sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r11.anchor: والثاني أن الملائكة تعرفهم بسيماهم فلا تسألهم عن ذنوبهم قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r12.claim: Qatada says they enter Hell without reckoning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r12.anchor: والثالث يدخلون النار بغير حساب قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r13.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says they are punished without being questioned about their sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p242/r13.anchor: وقال السدي يعذبون ولا يسألون عن ذنوبهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r1.claim: Qarun means God gave him wealth because God knew he deserved it and loved him; he rejects his people's counsel as unnecessary.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r1.anchor: أنا لا أفتقر إلى ما تقولون، فإن الله تعالى إنما أعطاني هذا المال لعلمه بأني أستحقه، ولمحبته لي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r2.claim: He compares Qarun's claim to people who say their prosperity proves they deserve it, citing 39:49 and 41:50.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r2.anchor: وهذا كقوله تعالى: {فإذا (1) مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r3.claim: Some interpret this as Qarun's knowledge of alchemy, but Ibn Kathir rejects it: alchemy is false, and no person can truly transmute substances by craft.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن بعضهم أنه أراد: {إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} أي: إنه كان يعاني علم الكيمياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r4.claim: Alchemists can only dye and disguise outward appearances; true transformation of created substances belongs to God, and no lawful proof validates the claimed art.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r4.anchor: وإنما يقدرون على الصبغ في الصورة الظاهرة، وهو كذب وزغل وتمويه، وترويج أنه صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r5.claim: A hadith qudsi condemns anyone who tries to create like God, challenging them to create an atom or a grain of barley.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r6.speaker: حيوة بن شريح المصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir allows miracles by God's will, citing Haywa ibn Shurayh turning a stone into red gold to aid a needy petitioner; this is God's act, not a craft.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p254/r6.anchor: كما روي عن حيوة بن شريح المصري، رحمه الله، أنه سأله سائل، فلم يكن عنده ما يعطيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r1.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r1.claim: Some say Qarun became wealthy because he knew the Greatest Name and invoked God with it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن قارون كان يعلم الاسم الأعظم، فدعا الله به، فتمول بسببه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the explanation that Qarun claimed God gave him wealth because he deserved it, rather than the alchemy or invocation explanations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r2.anchor: والصحيح المعنى الأول؛ ولهذا قال الله تعالى -رادا عليه فيما ادعاه من اعتناء الله به فيما أعطاه من المال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r3.claim: Qatada glosses Qarun's phrase as meaning that he had goodness or merit of his own.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: {على علم عندي} : على خير عندي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r4.claim: Al-Suddi understands Qarun to mean he knew he was entitled to the wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: على علم أني أهل لذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir praises Ibn Zayd's gloss: Qarun thought God's favor and recognition of his merit explained his wealth; the same presumption is made by people with little knowledge who see the rich.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r5.anchor: وقد أجاد في تفسير هذه الآية الإمام عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، فإنه قال في قوله: {قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي} قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r6.claim: Earlier peoples had greater strength and wealth, yet God destroyed them for disbelief and ingratitude; wealth does not prove divine love.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r6.anchor: أي: قد كان من هو أكثر منه مالا وما كان ذلك عن محبة منا له، وقد أهلكهم الله مع ذلك بكفرهم وعدم شكرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p255/r7.claim: The criminals are not asked about their sins because their sins are so numerous.

JISHUMI:v8p5534/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r3.claim: Claiming knowledge as one’s exclusive possession is blameworthy; knowledge should first be attributed to God, creator of necessary knowledge and source of acquired knowledge through its causes.
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r3.anchor: وتدل أن إضافة العلم إلى نفسه على وجه يتفرد به يقبح؛ بل يضاف أولا إليه تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r1.claim: Qārūn claims he deserved his wealth because of knowledge that distinguished him from others; he was said to be Israel’s most learned in the Torah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r1.anchor: على علم } أي على استحقاق واستيجاب لما في من العلم الذي فضلت به الناس ، وذلك أنه كان أعلم بني إسرائيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab reports that Moses taught alchemy in thirds to Joshua, Caleb, and Qārūn; Qārūn tricked the others into combining their shares and turned lead and copper into gold.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب : كان موسى عليه السلام يعلم علم الكيمياء ، فأفاد يوشع بن نون ثلثه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r3.claim: Another account says God taught Moses alchemy, Moses taught it to his sister, and she taught it to Qārūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : علم الله موسى علم الكيمياء ، فعلمه موسى أخته ، فعلمته أخته قارون .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r4.claim: A further explanation is that Qārūn meant knowledge of trade, farming, and other ways of earning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو بصره بأنواع التجارة والدهقنة وسائر المكاسب .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r5.claim: ʿIndī can mean in my opinion or estimation, as in saying something is so in one’s view; the wording resembles 39:49.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r5.anchor: { عندى } معناه : في ظني ، كا تقول الأمر عندي كذا ، كأنه قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r6.claim: One reading affirms that Qārūn knew from the Torah, Moses, and historians that stronger and richer peoples had been destroyed, so he should not have been deceived by wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون إثباتا لعلمه بأن الله قد أهلك من القرون قبله من هو أقوى منه وأغنى ، لأنه قد قرأه في التوراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the question denies that Qārūn possessed useful knowledge: he boasted of knowledge that supposedly made him deserve every blessing but failed to learn what could protect him from the fate of the dead.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نفيا لعلمه بذلك ؛ لأنه لما قال : أوتيته على علم عندي ، فتنفج بالعلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r8.claim: More in جمع can mean either greater wealth amassed or a larger company and number of people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r8.anchor: { وأكثر جمعا } للمال ، أو أكثر جماعة وعددا .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r9.claim: The clause threatens Qārūn: God sees criminals’ sins and needs no inquiry to learn them, and can punish them, as other verses state.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435#2/r9.anchor: قال على سبيل التهديد له : والله مطلع على ذنوب المجرمين ، لا يحتاج إلى سؤالهم عنها واستعلامهم . وهو قادر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says Qarun meant that he acquired his wealth through his own strength and knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r1.anchor: أحدها : أي بقوتي وعلمي , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r2.claim: Qatada says Qarun meant that he possessed goodness and knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r2.anchor: الثاني : علىخير وعلم عندي , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun meant that God favored him and knew he deserved the wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r3.anchor: الثالث : لرضا الله عني ومعرفته باستحقاقي , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r4.claim: Ibn Isa says Qarun meant that he knew how to conduct business and earn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r4.anchor: الرابع : على علم بوجه المكاسب , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that Qarun meant knowledge of alchemy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r5.anchor: الخامس : العلم بصنعة الكيمياء . حكى النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r6.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r6.claim: Al-Naqqash relates that Moses, Joshua, and Aaron's two sons each taught Qarun a third of alchemy; Qarun tricked the others, learned their shares, and grew wealthy by practicing it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r6.anchor: حكى النقاش أن موسى عليه السلام علم قارون الثلث من صنعة الكيمياء , وعلم يوشع بن نون الثلث

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r7.claim: Qatada says criminals are punished without being questioned or reckoned with.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r7.anchor: أحدها : يعذبون ولا يحاسبون , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r8.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r8.claim: Al-Rabi says they are not asked to enumerate their sins; instead, they receive their records, recognize them, and confess.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r8.anchor: الثاني : لا يسألون عن إحصائها ويعطون صحائفها فيعرفون ويعترفون بها , قاله الربيع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r9.claim: Mujahid says they are not asked because the angels recognize them by their marks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r9.anchor: الثالث : لأن الملائكة تعرفهم بسيماهم فلا تسأل عنهم , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r10.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r10.claim: Ibn Bahr says they are not asked to seek an excuse for why they did not believe, comparing the wording with 30:57.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p268/r10.anchor: الرابع : أنهم لا يسألون سؤال استعتاب : لم لم يؤمنوا , قاله ابن بحر

MUJAHID:v2p490#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p490#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p490#2/r1.claim: Mujahid links this to 55:41: wrongdoers are recognized by their marks, their faces blue-black, so the angels need not ask about them.
MUJAHID:v2p490#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون ﴾ قال هو كقوله ﴿ يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم ﴾ يعني زرقا سود الوجوه يقول الملائكة لا تسأل عنهم قد عرفتهم

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r9.claim: Qarun says his wealth was given to him on account of knowledge or good God knew to be in him.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r9.anchor: يقول: على خير علمه الله عز وجل عندي

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r10.claim: God destroyed earlier generations for rejecting their messengers, including people stronger and wealthier than Qarun, such as Nimrod.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r10.anchor: من قارون { قوة } وبطشا { وأكثر جمعا } من الأموال

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r11.claim: Criminals of this community are not asked about earlier nations’ sins, since God has recorded and knows their evil deeds.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r11.anchor: يقول: ولا يسأل مجرمو هذه الأمة عن ذنوب الأمم الخالية الذين عذبوا في الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r1.claim: The thing Qarun claims he was given is wealth.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r2.speaker: قارون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r2.claim: Qarun claims his wealth came through merit based on knowledge that distinguished him from other people, with possible meanings including Torah knowledge, alchemy, or expertise in trade and farming.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r2.anchor: أي على استحقاق لما في من العلم الذي فضلت به الناس وهو علم التوراة أو علم الكيمياء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r3.speaker: قارون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r3.claim: The author also lists knowledge of commercial and agricultural methods as Qarun's possible claim to have earned the wealth through his own expertise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r3.anchor: أو العلم بوجوه المكاسب من التجارة والزراعة وعندي صفة لعلم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r4.speaker: سهل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r4.claim: Sahl says no one prospers by admiring himself: the fortunate person sees God's favor in every deed and word, while the wretched person boasts of his own actions and is destroyed by that conceit, as Qarun was.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r4.anchor: قال سهل ما نظر أحد إلى نفسه فأفلح والسعيد من صرف بصره عن أفعاله وأقواله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r5.claim: One reading takes the question as affirming that Qarun knew from the Torah that God had destroyed earlier people stronger and richer than him, yet failed to learn from their fate.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r5.anchor: هو إثبات لعلمه بأن الله قد أهلك من القرون قبله من هو أقوى منه وأغنى لأنه قد قرأه في التوراة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the question denies Qarun had this useful knowledge: despite claiming superior knowledge and deserving every favor, he did not recognize the fate of the earlier powerful generations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r6.anchor: أو نفى لعلمه بذلك لأنه لما قال أوتيته على علم عندي قيل عنده مثل ذلك العلم الذي ادعاه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r7.claim: More abundant in collected wealth, or greater in followers and numbers.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r8.claim: Possible explanations: God already knows their sins, so they enter without reckoning; they confess without questioning; their marks identify them, though they may still be questioned in rebuke; or the verse concerns criminals of this community not being asked about earlier peoples' sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246#2/r8.anchor: لعلمه تعالى بهم بل يدخلون النار بغير حساب أو يعترفون بها بغير سؤال أو يعرفون بسيماهم فلا يسألون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r1.claim: Qarun means knowledge of the Torah; he was reportedly among its most learned readers and one of the seventy chosen by Moses for the meeting.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r1.anchor: يعني علم التوراة. وكان فيما روي من أقرأ الناس لها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun claimed God gave him wealth because God knew his merit and approved of him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r2.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أي إنما أوتيته لعلمه بفضلي ورضاه عني

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r3.claim: On Ibn Zayd’s reading, Qarun claims that God gave the treasures knowing he deserved them because of his virtue.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r3.anchor: معناه إن عندي أن الله تعالى آتاني هذه الكنوز على علم منه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r4.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa says Qarun meant his own knowledge of trade and earning.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r4.anchor: وقيل: أوتيته على علم من عندي بوجوه التجارة والمكاسب قاله علي بن عيسى

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r5.claim: Qarun failed to recognize that his wealth could not have accumulated without God making acquisition easy.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r5.anchor: ولم يعلم أن الله لو لم يسهل له اكتسابها لما اجتمعت عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun meant his knowledge of making gold, referring to alchemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: على علم عندي بصنعة الذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r7.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r7.claim: Al-Naqqash relates that Moses taught one third of alchemy to Qarun, who deceived Moses and Aaron to learn their portions and grew wealthy through it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r7.anchor: وحكى النقاش: أن موسى عليه السلام علمه الثلث من صنعة الكيمياء

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r8.claim: Another report says Moses taught alchemy to Joshua, Caleb ibn Yufanna, and Qarun.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى علم الكيمياء ثلاثة يوشع بن نون، وكالب بن يوفنا، وقارون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the Torah-knowledge explanation and rejects the alchemy explanation because alchemy is unreal.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r9.anchor: واختار الزجاج القول الأول، وأنكر قول من قال إنه يعمل الكيمياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r10.claim: A further story says Moses taught alchemy to his sister, Qarun’s wife, who taught Qarun.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى علم أخته علم الكيمياء، وكانت زوجة قارون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r11.claim: The destroyed generations were earlier unbelieving nations; Qarun should have known God destroys people stronger and wealthier than he.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r11.anchor: أي بالعذاب. { من القرون } أي الأمم الخالية الكافرة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r12.claim: Qarun’s predecessors had greater strength and amassed more wealth; if wealth proved merit, God would not have destroyed them.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r12.anchor: ولو كان المال يدل على فضل لما أهلكهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r13.claim: Another explanation takes strength as equipment and “gathering” as helpers and supporters.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r13.anchor: وقيل: القوة الآلات، والجمع الأعوان والأنصار

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r14.claim: The clause is a divine rebuke directed at Qarun.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r14.anchor: والكلام خرج مخرج التقريع من الله تعالى لقارون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r15.claim: The criminals are not questioned to solicit an apology or satisfaction; they are instead rebuked and blamed.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r15.anchor: لا يسألون سؤال استعتاب كما قال: ولا هم يستعتبون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r16.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r16.claim: Al-Hasan reconciles this with the statement that God will question everyone: questioning here is for rebuke, not to offer a chance to make amends.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r16.anchor: وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ لقوله: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r17.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r17.claim: Mujahid says angels will not need to ask about criminals, who are recognizable by their marks, including black faces and blue eyes.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r17.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا تسأل الملائكة غدا عن المجرمين فإنهم يعرفون بسيماهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r18.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r18.claim: Qatada says their sins are too obvious and numerous to require questioning, so they enter Hell without reckoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r18.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يسأل المجرمون عن ذنوبهم لظهورها وكثرتها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r19.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r19.claim: Another view says criminals of this community are not questioned about the sins of earlier nations punished in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r19.anchor: وقيل: لا يسأل مجرمو هذه الأمة عن ذنوب الأمم الخالية

QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r20.claim: Another explanation says God destroyed earlier peoples already knowing their sins, so He did not need to question them.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:78/r20.anchor: وقيل: أهلك من أهلك من القرون عن علم منه بذنوبهم
